articles.title: Aaron Rodgers vs Mike McCarthy: QB erupts on sideline at Mike McCarthy before finishing Steelers drive
articles.standfirst: Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy appeared to clash again on Thursday Night Football.
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy appeared to clash again on Thursday Night Football.
articles.body:
By now, Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy have played enough games together to give each other the benefit of the doubt. Even so, in their early days with the Steelers , they have appeared to be at odds at times.

Early in the 2026 season, Rodgers made comments about play calling that suggested the quarterback felt he needed to tell McCarthy how to run Pittsburgh's offense. With that unit among the NFL's lowest-scoring through three games, it hasn't all been pretty.

In Thursday night's matchup between the Browns and the Steelers , the two once again showed signs of tension: Rodgers appeared to scream expletives at his coach.

The argument between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy

The Steelers had a frustrating opening drive on "Thursday Night Football." It ended in a Roman Wilson touchdown , but it lasted about 10 minutes, with 17 plays and a seemingly endless string of penalties .

Before a 1st-and-10, Amazon's cameras focused on Pittsburgh's huddle. Rodgers was looking toward the sideline with his arms out to his sides, in a stance that indicated the play call hadn't come in yet.

"What the f***? CALL IT," Rodgers exclaimed.

"Fu**ing as*hole," McCarthy replied.

There are no deep-seated hard feelings between the two, given their history: McCarthy led the Packers to nine playoff appearances during Rodgers' time in Green Bay, including the 2010 Super Bowl title.

Still, Thursday's moment was the latest sign of communication problems between quarterback and coach, as the Steelers try to get their offense into a higher gear.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy regrets letting tempers flare with Aaron Rodgers: “I wish I wouldn’t use those words”
articles.standfirst: The Steelers coach said emotions boiled over during a chaotic opening drive
articles.summary: The Steelers coach said emotions boiled over during a chaotic opening drive
articles.body:
The Steelers ’ 27-24 defeat to the Browns was frustrating enough on its own, but the night also produced a familiar sight with Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy visibly arguing over the offense.

The exchange came during Pittsburgh’s opening drive, when Rodgers became impatient waiting for the next play call and yelled toward the sideline, “What the f**k, call it.” Television cameras then cut to McCarthy, who appeared to fire back: “F**king a**hole.”

After the game, McCarthy addressed the moment directly and acknowledged that he wished he had handled it differently.

“Communication, sometimes, is not the best choice of words,” McCarthy said. “Everybody’s competing on the field. But any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn’t use those words.”

First drive created unusual tension

The confrontation came during a long, 17-play possession that lasted more than nine minutes before Rodgers connected with Roman Wilson for a 12-yard touchdown.

McCarthy said the length and pace of the drive contributed to the communication problems.

“I know at the beginning of the game, first drive was hectic,” he said. “I was talking fast than normal. So, I think once we settled in after that drive, which resulted in a touchdown, I thought the communication was solid.”

The frustration didn't stop with Rodgers and McCarthy . T.J. Watt and Cam Heyward were also visibly upset with defensive calls at various points, with Watt even using a headset to communicate with defensive coordinator Patrick Graham .

Cleveland scored 21 points in the second quarter, putting Pittsburgh in a hole that became increasingly difficult to escape.

Green Bay history made moment stand out

Any public disagreement between Rodgers and McCarthy immediately brings their shared history back into focus.

The pair enjoyed enormous success with the Green Bay Packers , including a Super Bowl XLV title, multiple division championships and eight playoff appearances with Rodgers as the starting quarterback.

Their relationship also became strained over the years, particularly around play-calling and offensive philosophy, before McCarthy was fired during the 2018 season.

Rodgers has since described their time together as including both “amazing times” and periods when they “butted heads.”

Thursday night showed that competitive edge hasn't disappeared. Rodgers was sacked five times and threw two interceptions, including one on a desperation Hail Mary at the end of the game.

Pittsburgh also failed to score in the third quarter and spent most of the second half trying to recover from Cleveland’s surge. McCarthy ’s postgame regret may calm some of the attention around the viral exchange.

The bigger concern for Pittsburgh is whether the sideline frustration was simply a heated moment in a close divisional loss, or a sign of communication problems that need to be fixed quickly.

articles.title: Who is Amy Blunt? Alleged mother of Robert Citrone's son, the Steelers co-owner can't silence
articles.standfirst: The billionaire Steelers co-owner sought an emergency order after Blunt discussed their dispute online and with the media
articles.summary: The billionaire Steelers co-owner sought an emergency order after Blunt discussed their dispute online and with the media
articles.body:
What began as a private fight over child support has spilled into public view, with Amy Blunt and billionaire investor Robert Citrone now battling not only over money, but over what either side can say outside the courtroom.

Citrone recently asked a Pennsylvania judge to stop Blunt from discussing the dispute with journalists, newspapers or on social media. His attorneys argued that her posts about the case, his finances and their three-year-old son, Luca, violated earlier court restrictions.

The judge refused to impose the emergency order. The ruling doesn't mean everything in the case can now be made public. The underlying litigation remains sealed, and neither side is permitted to disclose confidential filings to people who are not involved in the proceedings.

What the judge did make clear is that no separate gag order currently prevents Blunt or Citrone from speaking about the dispute more generally.

Why are Amy Blunt and Robert Citrone in court?

Blunt is seeking access to Citrone ’s financial records as part of the child support case, including tax returns and income statements.

She has claimed Citrone earned about $113 million in taxable income in 2024 and argues that his finances are relevant to determining the proper level of support for Luca , who she says has significant medical needs.

Blunt has said Luca has Cornelia de Lange Syndrome and requires a wheelchair. A judge had already granted her permission to depose Citrone , his wife Cindy and his children about their lifestyle and standard of living.

The dispute became more heated after Blunt posted about the case online and indicated she planned to create a TikTok account discussing what she described as Citrone ’s alleged “infidelity and his refusal to support Luca.”

Citrone ’s legal team then sought to stop further public comments.

Blunt argues she has a right to speak

Blunt pushed back strongly against that request.

“Father just does not like Mother talking about him online, which is to say that he does not like the content of Mother’s speech,” she argued in response to the emergency filing.

She also maintained that “proscribing former romantic partners from speaking about their personal lives is not a ‘legitimate government interest.’”

Citrone is the co-founder of Discovery Capital Management and, alongside his wife, has held an ownership stake in the Steelers since 2009.

He and Cindy have also been involved in major philanthropic projects, including a multimillion-dollar commitment to Hampden-Sydney College.

The latest decision doesn't settle the underlying child support dispute. It does, however, represent an important procedural victory for Blunt , who can continue discussing the broader conflict publicly while the sealed financial and family issues remain before the court.

articles.body:
Mike Tomlin 's 12-year Minecraft project has produced an unsurprising question about the Pittsburgh Steelers coach once the scale was revealed: Was he spending too much time building a virtual city whilst his team struggled to in the NFL Playoffs ? The answer is not that simple, but Tomlin 's hobby has drawn criticism after he revealed the sprawling world he spent more than a decade creating whilst the Steelers slumped whenever it mattered.

​What began as a way to connect with his children eventually became an elaborate city-building project filled with hotels, apartments, sports venues, an aquarium and carefully designed public spaces as Tomlin described the project as therapeutic. The 54-year-old explained that it gave him an outlet away from the pressure of coaching one of the NFL 's most scrutinized franchises, yet some fans have questioned whether the time spent constructing his digital metropolis could have been better studying film. Tomlin 's Minecraft city was developed between roughly 2014 and 2025, a period in which the Steelers struggled to make a deep playoff run despite regularly fielding talented rosters. And the criticism reached the former Pittsburgh star Le'Veon Bell , who joked on X.com, formerly known as Twitter, “We were tryna win super bowls and coach T was on minecraft building cities.” That comment captured the tongue-in-cheek reaction from some fans, with one saying, "I was thinking the EXACT SAME THING... I just don't think Mike Macdonald or Andy Reid are up playing Minecraft at all hours...” The fan added: “I think Ben Johnson, Klint Kubiak, Liam Coen these guys are sleeping at the facility, studying film at 4 in the morning... I was truly kinda shocked."

Tomlin's Minecraft city is far more than a hobby

The reveal also showed why the project has attracted so much attention as Tomlin 's virtual city was built around a large body of water, with the coach explaining that he wanted the area to serve as the starting point for the entire development. His attention to detail quickly became apparent as one of the first buildings was a boutique hotel featuring an executive spa, therapy rooms and a multipurpose conference space. Tomlin even explained his preference for using glass ceilings to maximize natural light whilst the city includes an aquarium-themed apartment high-rise, a CVS and multiple sports facilities. He even built an MLS stadium and a baseball field designed to fit naturally into the surrounding cityscape, while also paying attention to which buildings offered the best views as even seemingly mundane details received attention. Tomlin discussed his focus on bedrooms and his desire to provide an appropriate number of public restrooms throughout office and multipurpose spaces, an obsession that would impress even video game designers. The 54-year-old coach has spent years creating something entirely unrelated to football and now faces criticism for that fact, but it cannot be forgot that he did win a Super Bowl with Pittsburgh in 2009 and they remained competitive throughout his tenure.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' life is about to change as he hints wife, Brittani, is pregnant
articles.standfirst: The 42-year-old quarterback gave fans a rare glimpse into the personal future he may be planning beyond the NFL
articles.summary: The 42-year-old quarterback gave fans a rare glimpse into the personal future he may be planning beyond the NFL
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has spent more than two decades preparing for Sundays, but when asked to picture his life a year from now, football was not part of the answer.

During a Prime Video conversation with Al Michaels before the Pittsburgh Steelers faced the Cleveland Browns , the 42-year-old quarterback was asked where he expected to be once his playing career had ended.

“I’ll either be tending to my pregnant wife or I’ll be taking care of my newborn,” Rodgers said.

The remark immediately drew attention because of how specific it was. Rodgers didn't simply mention spending more time at home with his wife, Brittani .

He directly referenced either a pregnancy or a newborn child. That has naturally fueled speculation, but neither Rodgers nor Brittani have publicly confirmed they're expecting a child.

Rodgers offered rare glimpse beyond football

Rodgers has already said the 2026 season will be his 22nd and final year in the NFL, making questions about life after football increasingly relevant.

He signed a one-year deal with the Steelers in May, reuniting with Mike McCarthy , his former coach with the Green Bay Packers . The move gave Rodgers one more season in the league before what is expected to be a permanent transition away from playing.

That context made his answer to Michaels particularly striking. Instead of talking about broadcasting, coaching or another football-related role, Rodgers pictured a much quieter future centered on family.

It was also notable because Rodgers has generally kept his relationship with Brittani private. Even when discussing his personal life publicly, he has offered relatively few details about their marriage.

Pregnancy speculation remains

Rodgers ’ wording leaves plenty of room for interpretation. It's possible he was speaking hypothetically about what he hopes the next stage of his life might look like.

Rodgers has also been known to use humor in interviews, meaning the comment should not be treated as an official announcement. What it does reveal is that fatherhood appears to be firmly on his mind.

After 22 seasons built around training camps, game plans, injuries and weekly preparation, Rodgers may be looking toward a very different routine once the season ends.

That shift would be significant for one of the NFL’s most recognizable quarterbacks. His answer suggested that retirement may not be defined by stepping away from football as much as stepping into something new.

articles.title: A $60M real estate deal: A look at three massive properties Aaron Rodgers is selling before retirement
articles.standfirst: The four-time NFL MVP has listed homes connected to different chapters of his football career
articles.summary: The four-time NFL MVP has listed homes connected to different chapters of his football career
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has accumulated more than $400 million in career earnings during his remarkable NFL journey, but the veteran quarterback is now attracting attention for the extraordinary real estate portfolio he is preparing to leave behind.

The Pittsburgh Steelers star has listed three properties with combined asking prices of $58.2 million, raising questions about how he intends to spend his time once his playing career ends.

The homes span California, New Jersey and Wisconsin, reflecting different periods of Rodgers ' career with the Green Bay Packers and New York Jets , as well as his life away from football.

According to Spotrac, the four-time NFL MVP has earned approximately $417.31 million over 22 seasons, providing the financial resources to invest in some of America's most exclusive properties.

Rodgers looks to cash in on Malibu mansion

Rodgers ' most valuable listing is his Malibu beachfront estate, which he purchased for $28 million in 2019 while dating former NASCAR driver Danica Patrick .

Now advertised for $39.5 million, the Mediterranean-inspired property includes a 4,625-square-foot main residence with four bedrooms and four bathrooms, alongside a separate two-bedroom guesthouse.

The luxurious coastal retreat also features a swimming pool, a private deck overlooking the Pacific Ocean and an outdoor fire pit surrounded by seating.

The listing describes the property as capturing "the essence of California coastal living through architectural refinement, privacy, and an effortless connection to the Pacific."

If the house sells for its asking price, the transaction would represent an $11.5 million increase over Rodgers ' original purchase price, before expenses.

Spectacular Manhattan skyline views

Another significant property is Rodgers ' contemporary mansion in Cedar Grove, New Jersey, which is being offered for $15 million.

The quarterback acquired the estate for approximately $9.5 million in 2023 after leaving Green Bay to join the Jets , creating an impressive residence overlooking Manhattan.

With eight bedrooms, nine-and-a-half bathrooms and a three-car garage, the house also includes a hot tub and sophisticated security technology.

"An extraordinary contemporary estate on the Cedar Grove/Montclair border commanding unobstructed views of the Manhattan skyline," the listing states.

Its distinctive glass-and-metal exterior provides panoramic views, while the extensive interior offers enough space for entertaining and private living.

Rodgers prepares to part with Wisconsin retreat

The third home carries considerably more personal history, having served as Rodgers ' primary residence during much of his successful tenure in Green Bay.

Located in Hobart, Wisconsin, the four-bedroom estate has been listed for $3.7 million since November 2025, offering approximately 10,500 square feet of living space.

The property sits on 5.32 acres of landscaped grounds, providing the privacy Rodgers enjoyed while establishing himself as one of the NFL's most accomplished quarterbacks.

Its listing describes a "custom-built all-stone estate" surrounded by secluded greenery, reflecting the quieter lifestyle available away from the football spotlight.

Although Rodgers hasn't publicly connected the sales to a confirmed retirement decision, the listings come as his career approaches its conclusion.

Whether all three properties attract buyers remains uncertain, but their combined asking prices underline the extraordinary wealth Rodgers has accumulated through football.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers has another historic record within reach. Which legend could he surpass?
articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback has climbed to third on the all-time passing touchdown list and is now 26 scores away from another milestone.
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback has climbed to third on the all-time passing touchdown list and is now 26 scores away from another milestone.
articles.body:
At 42, Aaron Rodgers continues to find reasons to extend a career that has already made him one of the NFL’s most accomplished quarterbacks . Although his retirement from football may be getting closer, the Pittsburgh Steelers star still has records to chase. His latest milestone came with 582 passing touchdowns in the regular season and playoffs combined , a total that moved him into sole possession of third place on the all-time list and put another major target within reach.

​Aaron Rodgers moves past Peyton Manning

The record took shape during the Steelers’ 34-22 victory over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, October 11 . In the first quarter, Rodgers connected with running back Jaylen Warren for an 80-yard touchdown, allowing him to surpass the 579 passing touchdowns Peyton Manning recorded over his career.

But Rodgers wasn’t finished there. In the same game, he connected with Pat Freiermuth twice to bring his total to 582 touchdowns, adding scores in the second and fourth quarters.

Drew Brees is next on the list

With 582 passing touchdowns across the regular season and playoffs, Rodgers is now 26 touchdowns away from tying Drew Brees’ mark of 608 and 27 away from surpassing him .

Above them both sits Tom Brady, who leads the all-time rankings with 737 passing touchdowns . That record presents a much bigger challenge, but Brees is Rodgers’ next major target.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' estranged brother shares adorable videos of QB with his kids confirming everything has changed
articles.standfirst: Is the Pittsburgh Steelers’ quarterback healing his broken bond with his family?
articles.summary: Is the Pittsburgh Steelers’ quarterback healing his broken bond with his family?
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers ’ relationship with his family appears to have taken another positive turn, with his brother Luke sharing heartwarming footage of the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback spending time with his niece and nephew during a recent game at Acrisure Stadium.

The Instagram carousel, posted Sunday, captured Rodgers posing with the children in Steelers gear, chatting with his niece and watching the young fans cheer from a stadium suite against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5.

Their presence offered another glimpse of a family relationship that has improved after years of estrangement as Luke captioned the post, “Last weekend was pretty special,” accompanied by black and gold heart emojis.

The 42-year-old Rodgers also left a comment, writing, “Planes, trains and renegade. Also misspelled cakes.”

The photos included a particularly tender moment in which Rodgers crouched down to interact with his niece, who wore a pink jacket over a Steelers jersey, and other clips showed the children waving Terrible Towels and celebrating from the stands as they supported their uncle.

Luke and his wife, Aimee , welcomed their third child in August, making the family gathering another significant moment amid the gradual rebuilding of relationships that had been strained for years.

A major sign of progress arrived in July, when Rodgers shared photographs from a family “bonding week.”

The images surprised fans who had followed the long-running dispute and suggested that private efforts to reconnect were beginning to produce visible results.

Rodgers stars in overtime victory over Steelers

On the field, Rodgers threw for 253 yards and two touchdowns as the Pittsburgh Steelers overcame a 13-point fourth-quarter deficit to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 26-19 in overtime, securing their first road victory of the season and improving to 4-2.

Super Bowl-winning quarterback finished 33 of 49 passing despite being sacked five times during the opening three quarters as Pittsburgh struggled to find the end zone, until the veteran sparked the comeback with a five-yard touchdown pass to Darnell Washington early in the fourth quarter.

Rodgers then connected with Germie Bernard on a seven-yard touchdown pass with 3:15 remaining in overtime, capping a 12-play, 70-yard drive that put Pittsburgh ahead for good.

His two scoring passes also brought his career total to 539, tying Peyton Manning for third on the NFL's all-time list as the Steelers defense completed the victory when Jalen Ramsey sacked Tampa Bay rookie Jalon Daniels on fourth down during the visitor’s final possession.

“These are the most important moments for us as a team to grow. This is a trajectory win,” Rodgers said, post-game. “You can go to 3-3 and then you've got a Paris trip... and that's just not what you want to do, obviously.

“To be 4-2, to win our first road game... to beat a team we should've beat... there's no two ways about it, you've got to beat teams like that if you want to get where we want to get.”

Rodgers ' performance helped Pittsburgh recover from a difficult start against a Buccaneers defense that recorded five sacks as the team remains firmly in contention in the AFC North.

articles.title: The truth about Aaron Rodgers' family reunion: Why it's not as perfect as he claims
articles.standfirst: Steelers quarterback's relationship with younger brother Jordan remains complicated despite their reconciliation.
articles.summary: Steelers quarterback's relationship with younger brother Jordan remains complicated despite their reconciliation.
articles.body:
A recent family gathering at a Pittsburgh Steelers game appeared to represent a significant turning point for Aaron Rodgers , whose strained relationship with his relatives has attracted public attention for years.

His parents, Ed and Darla Rodgers , attended alongside older brother Luke Rodgers , providing a visible sign that the quarterback had made progress toward repairing relationships once thought to be deeply fractured.

However, one family member was notably missing from the occasion: younger brother Jordan Rodgers , who has maintained a complicated relationship with Aaron since their falling-out became public in 2016.

According to an anonymous source who spoke to Page Six, the brothers have resumed some communication, but their relationship has not necessarily returned to normal.

"JoJo [Fletcher] and Jordan are cordial with Aaron," the source claimed. "It seems like Aaron has led the public to believe things are better than they actually are with Jordan."

The latest claims contrast with the optimistic picture Aaron recently presented when discussing his family relationships on the Not Just Football podcast.

The four-time NFL MVP explained that rebuilding those connections had required separate conversations with his parents and each of his brothers.

"There were tough conversations for sure," Rodgers acknowledged. "But I'm just in a much better headspace."

Rodgers also credited his wife, Brittani , with helping him navigate the reconciliation, although he has continued keeping details of their marriage largely private.

The quarterback's comments suggested that important progress had been made, but he did not claim every disagreement within the family had been completely resolved.

The source told Page Six that Jordan and his wife, JoJo Fletcher , remain reluctant to discuss the situation.

"It still seems like a very sensitive topic for Jordan," the insider said.

Why Aaron and Jordan Rodgers stopped speaking

The brothers' estrangement became public during the 2016 season of The Bachelorette, when Jordan introduced Fletcher to his family.

Aaron was absent from the televised hometown visit, prompting questions about why the NFL quarterback was not participating.

"Me and Aaron don't really have that much of a relationship," Jordan explained at the time.

"It's just kind of the way he's chosen to do life, and I've chosen to stay close with my family and my parents and [Luke]."

The comments exposed a family disagreement that subsequently remained unresolved in public for years.

Although Aaron has recently described efforts to reconnect, neither brother has provided a detailed account of their current relationship.

Absence from Steelers game has another explanation

Jordan 's absence from the recent family reunion attracted attention, but the Page Six source insisted that geography and professional commitments were important factors.

Jordan and Fletcher live in Puerto Rico with their daughter, Romy, and reportedly prefer limiting travel whenever possible.

"JoJo and Jordan's location has a lot to do with not seeing the family as much," the source explained.

The insider also emphasized that Jordan remains extremely close to his parents, despite not attending every family gathering.

"Jordan is really busy with work, so even if everything between him and his family was good, it isn't odd he isn't at games supporting Aaron all of the time," the source added.

The contrast between Aaron 's positive reflections and the source's more cautious account indicates that the reconciliation may still be developing.

After years of estrangement, the brothers appear to have made progress, but the full extent of their renewed relationship remains known primarily to the family itself.

articles.standfirst: The legendary NFL quarterback refused to answer questions about tension within his family for a long time, but reconnected with them in 2026.
articles.summary: The legendary NFL quarterback refused to answer questions about tension within his family for a long time, but reconnected with them in 2026.
articles.body:
For years, it was known by just about everyone that Aaron Rodgers had a very delicate family situation. Even comedians referenced a “hatred” for his family, with Rodgers portraying a football-first persona on the field and off the field. Rodgers himself avoided questions when asked about it.

As Rodgers prepared for his 22nd NFL season , at 42 years old , something within him sparked a change. Over the summer, Rodgers posted a slideshow of pictures with family members, captioning the post, “ Another bonding week. #fam ”. The post sparked intrigue, and Rodgers later explained through the media that he’s been trying to get over the previous turmoil.

Many different things led to Rodgers’ estrangement from his family, particularly in the 2010s. From clashing religious and spiritual beliefs, to the changing landscape of Rodgers’ life due to newfound fame, to disagreements over his relationship with Olivia Munn , there was a lot that went wrong.

It all seemingly came to a head when his brother, Jordan Rodgers, had a scene on The Bachelorette in 2016 where Aaron’s absence was symbolized by an empty chair at a dinner table. Aaron felt betrayed by the stunt. There were bitter feelings festering before then, but that put everything over the top.

Now in his 40s, Rodgers is leaving the hurt behind in order to be a better human, better family member, and better husband to the mysterious Brittani . articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' criticism of the NFL over the Jalen Hurts case: “I can't say I'm surprised”
articles.standfirst: Hurts has been diagnosed with a blood clot following a clash with the Jacksonville Jaguars
articles.summary: Hurts has been diagnosed with a blood clot following a clash with the Jacksonville Jaguars
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers has questioned the NFL' s handling of Jalen Hurts ' medical situation, saying his own history with the league's chief medical officer, Dr. Allen Sills , leaves him unsurprised by the controversy surrounding the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback.

Hurts has been diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and blood clots in both lungs, a serious development that has raised questions about how he was cleared to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London .

And the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback expressed concern for his fellow quarterback whilst simultaneously acknowledging that he did not know all the details of the situation.

“I don’t have a close relationship with Jalen,” Rodgers said. “Obviously, we’re in the quarterback fraternity, so you don’t want to see anything like that happen to anybody. Especially a guy who’s still in football.

“Obviously, I don’t know all the details about what’s going on. All I’ve seen is what’s been printed. Allen Sills, he’s the guy in charge of all things medical at the NFL office. And he and I haven’t always seen eye-to-eye about things. So, I can’t say I’m real surprised.”

The veteran's remarks come amid growing scrutiny of the Eagles ' medical decisions as Hurts was reportedly diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in his left calf shortly before the October 11 game against the Jaguars .

However, he was controversially cleared to play and finished with 222 passing yards and a touchdown in Philadelphia 's 19-17 defeat in the United Kingdom as reports subsequently claimed Hurts had been instructed to remain awake overnight and had gone roughly 36 hours without sleep before taking the field.

But the NFL disputed that account, describing it as misinformation and clarifying that the team had encouraged personnel to remain awake during the journey home from London to maintain their usual routines.

“That was not true and no one told him not to sleep because of his situation,” NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy said. “The club told all players, coaches and personnel to try to stay awake as long as they could on Saturday as the team was returning back home after the game in London.

“The team did not have a bye week and like other NFL teams that travel to London and back, they were trying maintain as much of a normal routine as possible.”

Hurts' diagnosis raises serious medical questions

Further examinations reportedly revealed that the clots had progressed as Hurts was ruled out for the following game, placed on injured reserve and subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the season, according to reports.

Deep vein thrombosis occurs when a clot forms in a deep vein, commonly in the leg. A pulmonary embolism develops when a clot travels to the lungs, potentially becoming life-threatening.

And Hurts ' representatives and the Eagles have said his prognosis is very good and that they anticipate a full recovery, with treatment involving blood thinners as the NFL Players Association has called for a full investigation into the circumstances surrounding the quarterback's treatment.

However, the league has indicated it does not plan to investigate the medical care Hurts received, whilst Sills has defended the medical staff's handling of the situation, whilst the Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has also faced questions as pressure mounts.

articles.title: Bonjour, Pittsburgh! Aaron Rodgers and Steelers Top Saints in Historic Paris Showdown
articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 at the Stade de France
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers defeat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 at the Stade de France
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers led the Pittsburgh Steelers this Sunday to a 16-10 victory over the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular-season game in history played in Paris .

In the game, which was played without incident at the Stade de France , Rodgers, a four-time season MVP, passed for 212 yards and a touchdown pass.

With the victory, their third consecutive, the Steelers moved to five wins and two losses atop the American Conference North division , while the Saints fell to 2-5 in third place in the National Conference South.

The Steelers' offense got off to a dominant start against the Saints' defense, which they dragged for 51 yards in eight plays with Jaylen Warren as the battering ram who accounted for 43 of those yards , but they bogged down inside the red zone and had to settle for a 28-yard field goal that Chris Boswell converted to take a 3-0 lead .

In the second quarter, Tyler Shough moved the Saints' offense on a drive that covered 62 yards so that Daniel Carlson tied the game 3-3 after connecting on a 38-yard field goal .

The Pittsburgh team regained the lead (10-3) with a pass from Aaron Rodgers to the end zone that Darnell Washington caught , in a drive in which a 51-yard connection from Rodgers to DK Metcalf was key, leaving his team inside the Saints' five-yard line.

Third quarterback with the most touchdown passes

With this scoring pass, Rodgers became the third quarterback with the most "touchdown" passes in NFL history , with 540, still far behind Drew Brees , second with the most touchdown passes, with 571, and Tom Brady , first, with 649.

The New Orleans team reestablished its offense, which drove 51 yards to Devaughn Vele's touchdown, as he caught a pass from Shough that tied the game at 10-10.

The Steelers went into halftime with a 13-10 lead after Chris Boswell made a 47-yard field goal in the final second of the period.

At the start of the third quarter, the Saints chewed up half the clock on a drive that threatened to end in a touchdown, but at the 10-yard line from the end zone Shough was intercepted by Payton Wilson, a big play that the Steelers' offense turned into three more points, 16-10, with a Boswell field goal that proved to be the game-winner .

Before the start of this game, Roger Goodell, the NFL commissioner, said he had no doubt that the league will return to Paris with another regular-season game.

Goodell said this despite the fact that the NFL canceled several fan activities the previous Saturday due to the protests that the French capital has been repeatedly experiencing for the past couple of weeks.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers finds the path to happiness, and the Steelers won't be able to change their minds about his future
articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is enjoying a successful season, but his determination to retire after the 2026 campaign could remain unchanged even if the team makes a deep playoff run
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is enjoying a successful season, but his determination to retire after the 2026 campaign could remain unchanged even if the team makes a deep playoff run
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers appears to have found the right situation to enjoy the final chapter of his NFL career.

The 42-year-old quarterback is helping the Pittsburgh Steelers compete in 2026, adding to his historic achievements while working again with former Green Bay Packers head coach Mike McCarthy .

Despite his recent success, Rodgers has maintained that this will be his final season. The Steelers may hope a strong finish convinces him to reconsider, but the veteran appears comfortable with his decision to walk away.

Pittsburgh improved to 5-2 after defeating the New Orleans Saints 16-10 in Paris on Sunday, October 25.

Rodgers contributed to the victory while moving past Peyton Manning on the NFL's all-time career passing touchdown list, adding another milestone to an already remarkable career.

For Rodgers , however, the season appears to be about more than statistics. His return to Pittsburgh followed an uncertain period after the 2025 campaign, when retirement seemed a realistic possibility.

The opportunity to reunite with McCarthy , who coached him for 13 seasons in Green Bay, ultimately helped bring him back for one more year.

Rodgers insists his retirement decision will stand

When Rodgers confirmed his return in May, he was direct about his intentions for the future.

“Yes. This is it,” he said when asked whether the 2026 season would be his last.

The statement left little room for speculation. Although the Steelers have given him a competitive environment and the opportunity to pursue another championship, Rodgers has shown no clear indication that he intends to extend his career beyond the current campaign.

His reunion with McCarthy has played an important role in making this final season appealing.

The pair won Super Bowl XLV with the Packers, and working together again has offered Rodgers the chance to finish his career alongside a coach who understands his strengths.

Pittsburgh's progress could nevertheless create a difficult temptation. A deep postseason run, particularly one ending with a Super Bowl victory, would provide an unforgettable conclusion to Rodgers ' career.

But the quarterback has already experienced the highs of winning a championship and collecting individual honours, meaning another achievement may not be enough to change his priorities.

The Steelers must make the most of their opportunity

Rodgers remains productive, recording 13 touchdown passes, five interceptions and 1,699 passing yards through his first seven games of the season.

His latest victory also reinforced his ability to help Pittsburgh navigate difficult contests, even when the offense struggles to find consistency.

The Steelers ' defense has also helped the team maintain a strong start, giving Rodgers a platform to compete without needing to produce spectacular numbers every week.

That balance could prove crucial during the playoffs, when Pittsburgh will hope its veteran quarterback's experience makes the difference in close games.

Another championship would be an ideal ending, but the franchise cannot build its future around the assumption that Rodgers will return.

For now, Rodgers appears content with his decision. He has reunited with a trusted coach, found a competitive team and given himself another opportunity to chase success.

The Steelers can make his final season memorable, but they cannot decide what comes next. Unless Rodgers changes his mind, Pittsburgh must prepare for life after its veteran quarterback, regardless of how far the team progresses in January.

articles.title: “My entire family could've been killed in a plane crash, and I could have played”: Terry Bradshaw reveals lengths NFL went to protect him from depression
articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh Steelers legend has explained how football provided an escape from emotional struggles that began during college
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers legend has explained how football provided an escape from emotional struggles that began during college
articles.body:
Winning four Super Bowls made Terry Bradshaw one of the most celebrated quarterbacks in NFL history, but the former Pittsburgh Steelers star has revealed that some of his greatest personal struggles unfolded while he was still playing.

The 78-year-old Hall of Famer has spoken candidly about living with depression, explaining how the football field offered an escape from emotions he struggled to understand throughout his younger years.

During an appearance on the 10% Happier with Dan Harris podcast, Bradshaw recalled how completely the sport occupied his attention, allowing him to temporarily separate himself from problems outside the game.

"When I'm on the field playing, my entire family could've been killed in a plane crash, and I could have played," Bradshaw said. "Because that's where I found my happy place."

Bradshaw explained that his difficulties with depression began during college and continued throughout his NFL career, although he initially lacked an understanding of what he was experiencing.

One particularly painful moment occurred after he was sacked shortly before halftime during a Steelers game.

Instead of immediately returning to his feet, the quarterback remained on the ground as years of suppressed emotions suddenly overwhelmed him.

"I just sat there, trying to get it together, but it just emptied. It just emptied on me," Bradshaw recalled.

Team trainer Ralph Berlin and other medical staff approached him, initially believing he had suffered an injury.

However, Bradshaw was crying rather than recovering from a physical blow, leaving the staff to help him regain his composure without drawing attention to what was happening.

When he eventually stood up, supporters cheered, apparently assuming the quarterback had overcome an injury.

The reality was considerably different, with Bradshaw experiencing an emotional crisis that remained unknown to those watching.

Why NFL success could not prevent depression

Bradshaw 's struggles continued despite enjoying one of the most successful careers of his generation.

He led Pittsburgh to four Super Bowl victories, claimed two Super Bowl MVP awards and received the NFL's Most Valuable Player honor in 1978.

Across 14 seasons, he accumulated 27,989 passing yards and 212 touchdowns before entering the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1989.

Yet Bradshaw explained that professional achievements didn't eliminate his emotional difficulties, which could return even when his personal circumstances appeared positive.

Wife Tammy helped recognize depression

The former quarterback revealed that his wife, Tammy Bradshaw , has developed a simple way of helping him recognize when depression is affecting him.

The couple refer to the condition as "Roy," with Tammy asking whether Roy has returned whenever she notices changes in her husband's behavior.

Bradshaw also reflected on the importance of family when discussing his decision to step away from television commitments following his father's death.

"I wasn't going to do a Super Bowl. Somebody else can take my place, and somebody else can present the trophy, but I'm here for my family," he said.

His reflections offer a poignant reminder that even the most successful athletes can experience profound emotional difficulties, often hidden behind the performances that define their public lives.

articles.title: Tom Brady admits Aaron Rodgers isn’t the same quarterback anymore
articles.standfirst: Tom Brady believes Aaron Rodgers has changed at 42, but the NFL legend explains why the Steelers QB is still winning games.
articles.summary: Tom Brady believes Aaron Rodgers has changed at 42, but the NFL legend explains why the Steelers QB is still winning games.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are enjoying a strong run with Aaron Rodgers as their starting quarterback, winning four straight games, but Tom Brady believes the veteran is no longer the same player who dominated the NFL during the peak of his career.

For the seven-time Super Bowl champion , Rodgers has had to transform his style of play over the years. While he has lost some of his explosiveness when escaping pressure and extending plays, Brady believes the Pittsburgh quarterback has found a new way to remain an effective signal-caller.

During his Tuesday appearance on The Herd with Colin Cowherd , the former New England Patriots quarterback explained how Rodgers has evolved, defended his performance despite his interceptions, and made a strong prediction about the Steelers’ future in the AFC North .

Tom Brady highlights the change in Aaron Rodgers’ game

Brady pointed out that one of the biggest differences between the current version of Rodgers and the one who starred with the Green Bay Packers is his ability to create plays outside of the offensive structure.

“He doesn’t quite have that same elusiveness, and he’s really transitioned to becoming more of a pocket passer. He’s always been an incredible passer of the football, but now that he’s playing from the pocket, he’s totally in control.”

For years, Rodgers was known for his ability to extend plays, escape defensive pressure, and create opportunities when a play appeared to break down. However, that part of his game has declined with age, especially after the Achilles injury that ended his 2023 season with the New York Jets after just four snaps.

The statistics reflect that transformation. Through eight games this season, Rodgers has recorded just 12 rushing attempts for 23 yards . In 16 games with Pittsburgh in 2025 , he totaled 61 rushing yards after posting 107 yards with the Jets in 2024 .

Brady understands that adjustment process well. The legendary quarterback played until he was 45 years old and also relied more on reading defenses, anticipation, and accuracy rather than athletic ability to escape defenders.

Brady defends Rodgers after his six interceptions

Beyond discussing his mobility, Brady also defended Rodgers amid criticism surrounding his turnovers.

“I think he’s got six interceptions this year; five of them have been off the hands of a receiver or a Hail Mary. So he’s making incredible decisions.”

Rodgers has completed 60.8% of his passes for 1,871 yards , 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions in eight starts this season. Brady believes several of those turnovers do not necessarily reflect poor decisions by the quarterback.

One example came in Pittsburgh’s recent 27-6 win over Cleveland , when a pass intended for DK Metcalf bounced off the receiver’s hands and was intercepted by Denzel Ward . Metcalf finished the game with just one reception for four yards on six targets.

Rodgers finished that matchup with 13 completions on 25 attempts for 172 yards , no touchdowns, and one interception. The Steelers made up for the performance with a dominant rushing attack that produced 200 yards, including 143 from Brady defends Rodgers after his six interceptions, along with a defense that recorded eight sacks.

Tom Brady believes Steelers can dominate the AFC North

Although Rodgers no longer has the same mobility he showed during his prime years, Brady believes his football intelligence and decision-making ability are still enough to keep Pittsburgh competitive.

The Steelers improved to 6-2 and moved into sole possession of first place in the AFC North before their bye week. According to Brady, the team has what it takes to stay at the top.

“That’s why that team is in first place in their division, and I don’t see anybody stopping them in that division either,” Brady said.

Pittsburgh will return to action on November 15 against Cincinnati . While Rodgers’ style of play has changed, Brady believes the veteran quarterback still has the tools needed to lead a contender.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy's striking comment on Mike Tomlin's mood: “I've never seen him smile so much”
articles.standfirst: Former Steelers coach seems happier than ever after leaving the sidelines
articles.summary: Former Steelers coach seems happier than ever after leaving the sidelines
articles.body:
Mike Tomlin appears to be enjoying a refreshing change of pace after walking away from one of the NFL's most demanding coaching positions.

According to his successor in Pittsburgh , Mike McCarthy , the former Steelers head coach has been showing a side of himself that wasn't particularly familiar during his years on the sidelines.

McCarthy recently spoke about Tomlin's transition into television, admitting that his former coaching rival seems happier than ever. His observation was particularly funny given Tomlin's reputation for maintaining an intense presence throughout his 19-year tenure in Pittsburgh.

“I'm really happy for Mike. I'm trying not to laugh because I've never seen him smile so much. I'm told he's very happy. He's doing a great job,” McCarthy told reporters. He also expressed hope that the two would meet in Cincinnati.

articles.standfirst: After years of estrangement, Rodgers and his younger brother Jordan have finally been pictured together again
articles.summary: After years of estrangement, Rodgers and his younger brother Jordan have finally been pictured together again
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers has shared a rare photograph with younger brother Jordan , offering another indication that their long-running family feud is finally becoming a thing of the past as the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback reunited with him at Acrisure Stadium on Friday Posing arm-in-arm with the Super Bowl winner, Jordan was in the city working as a college football analyst for the game between the Pittsburgh Panthers and Florida State Seminoles as Rodgers took the opportunity to celebrate his younger brother's professional achievements.

"Great to see little bro @jrodgers11 in his element tonight @acrisurestadium. Really proud of how hard he’s worked to get to where he is now," Aaron wrote alongside the picture, sharing their photograph on Instagram as the reunion carries considerable significance given the history between the brothers. Their estrangement became public in 2016, when Jordan appeared on The Bachelorette and revealed that Aaron would not attend his hometown visit because they were no longer on speaking terms before subsequently criticized his younger brother for discussing private family matters on television. Calling it "a little inappropriate" in July 2016 whilst playing for the Green Bay Packers , Rodgers ’ relationship with his sibling remained strained for years, with the NFL star also missing Jordan and JoJo Fletcher 's wedding in Mexico in 2022. The quarterback subsequently revealed that he had also met with Jordan after reconnecting with the rest of his family as he acknowledged that the conversations had not always been easy. "A couple weeks after that, I met with my little brother. It was cool. There were tough conversations for sure, but I’m just in a much better headspace," Rodgers explained as he described the family being back together as "amazing" and credited his wife with helping him reach a position where repairing those relationships became possible.

Rodgers faces crucial Steelers-Bengals showdown after family reconciliation

Jordan had also offered a rare public show of support on November 4, selecting Aaron when asked on ESPN 's First Take which AFC quarterback he would trust most in the playoffs and the settled feud between Rodgers and his family comes at a pivotal time for the veteran. Rodgers prepares for a major AFC North contest as Pittsburgh visits the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 15, with both teams entering Week 10 at 6-2 and competing for outright possession of first place in the division. The Steelers won the first meeting 30-27 on September 27, giving them an opportunity to secure the head-to-head advantage with another victory - however, Cincinnati arrives having won four consecutive games, including a 34-17 victory in Madrid . Rodgers will face Joe Burrow in an important divisional matchup, with kickoff scheduled for 20:20 ET/17:20 PT at the Paycor Stadium as the game will be broadcast on NBC and Peacock.

articles.title: In 2013, Mike Tomlin was involved in a controversial incident with Jacoby Jones against the Ravens that cost him $100,000: 13 years later, he still hasn't forgotten it
articles.standfirst: Tomlin caused much controversy in a game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore
articles.summary: Tomlin caused much controversy in a game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore
articles.body:
Thirteen years after a controversial moment against the Baltimore Ravens , Mike Tomlin has revisited the incident that resulted in a $100,000 NFL fine as the former Pittsburgh Steelers coach insists he never intended to interfere with Jacoby Jones , despite the footage that made him one of the game's biggest talking points. The incident took place on December 2, 2013, during the third quarter of Pittsburgh ’s matchup with the Ravens . After the Steelers scored, Jones gathered the kickoff and raced downfield, only to approach Tomlin , who was standing close to the sideline area.

Jones completed a 73-yard return, but replays quickly made Tomlin the focus as the coach appeared on the stadium jumbotron smiling as the Ravens player approached, prompting questions about whether he had deliberately moved into the returner’s route to slow him down. “It broke my stride a little bit. I still shouldn't have got caught,” Jones said after the game as his comments offered a measure of context from the player involved, but the episode remained a defining and costly controversy for Tomlin and the Steelers .

Why did Tomlin get a fine and what was his excuse?

And speaking on the Not Just Football podcast, Tomlin explained that the stadium’s video screen left him disoriented as he watched the return unfold as he suddenly noticed himself on the display and moved to his left because he feared Jones was about to run directly into him. Tomlin said that his usual routine was to speak with the kickoff unit before the play, then stand near the kick-off yard line to check whether his players were onside. Once the ball was in motion, he watched the stadium screen for its wider view. He explained that Baltimore ’s stadium had only one jumbotron, making it difficult to judge where he stood while following the play. When he noticed himself on the screen, he moved left because he feared Jones was about to run directly into him on the sideline. “The truth didn't save me from a fine,” Tomlin said. “I got fined a hundred thousand dollars after the ball was kicked. Spatially, I get disoriented where I am and I'm watching something that I don't want to happen.” The NFL did not accept Tomlin ’s explanation or Jones ’ added context as grounds to avoid discipline as after reviewing the footage, the league fined the head coach $100,000. He was punished standing too close to the field and interfering with the return, while officials considered an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty. Pittsburgh was also warned that the incident could lead to the loss of draft picks in the 2014 NFL Draft - although no selections were ultimately taken away after Tomlin was handed the fine.

articles.title: Fed-up Aaron Rodgers appears to threaten to quit Steelers in foul-mouthed tirade during Bengals rout
articles.standfirst: Steelers star sparks retirement speculation after heated outburst during Bengals blowout
articles.summary: Steelers star sparks retirement speculation after heated outburst during Bengals blowout
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers had a disastrous evening in Cincinnati, and his growing frustration became one of the biggest talking points after the Pittsburgh Steelers suffered a crushing 38-18 defeat to the Bengals on Sunday Night Football.

The veteran quarterback was visibly angry throughout the divisional clash, repeatedly directing angry comments towards teammates and gesturing towards the sideline as Pittsburgh struggled to find any offensive rhythm.

The Steelers entered the contest with a 6-2 record, but their performance was a significant disappointment. Cincinnati, meanwhile, produced an outstanding display led by Joe Burrow, who threw for 409 yards and four touchdowns to help his team strengthen its position at the top of the AFC North.

Rodgers managed just 143 passing yards from 15 completions on 29 attempts, with Pittsburgh's offense looking ineffective during the opening three quarters. The Steelers had accumulated only 33 total yards by that stage, while Rodgers endured a difficult start that saw him fail to complete his first eight passes.

His frustration eventually spilled over in several heated moments that attracted attention on social media. During one intense outburst, some NFL fans believed they heard the 42-year-old declare, "I want to [expletive] quit."

However, viewers weren't entirely convinced about what Rodgers actually said. Others interpreted the same footage as him shouting, "You got to [expletive] want it," and maybe directing his anger towards Pittsburgh's receiving group.

Although neither interpretation has been confirmed, the incident highlighted just how difficult the evening had become for the four-time MVP.

Rodgers' frustration contrasts with postgame respect for Burrow

The quarterback was also reportedly heard demanding that someone on the sideline "get me a guard" as Cincinnati's defensive pressure continued to cause problems. Rodgers was sacked three times and struggled to establish any consistency against the Bengals defense.

It wasn't the first time this season that his temper has attracted attention. During Pittsburgh's October Thursday Night Football meeting with the Cleveland Browns, Rodgers became involved in an apparent foul-mouthed exchange with head coach Mike McCarthy.

While waiting for the next play call, Rodgers appeared to shout, "What the [expletive]? Call it!" Cameras subsequently captured McCarthy seemingly responding with an equally colorful remark.

Despite the frustration and disappointing result in Cincinnati, Rodgers produced a much more gracious moment after the final whistle.

Meeting Burrow at midfield, the Steelers quarterback acknowledged his opponent's outstanding performance, telling him, "That was a clinic out there, kid."

Burrow responded with a heartfelt message of his own, saying, "If this is your last one, much love and respect."

The exchange carried significance given the uncertainty surrounding Rodgers ' NFL future and the possibility that his playing career could soon come to an end.

While his emotional reactions dominated much of the broadcast, the postgame interaction showed the respect between two accomplished quarterbacks.

articles.title: Paige Spiranac baffles NFL fans by revealing which teams she supports
articles.standfirst: The golf influencer shared a video to promote a new clothing collection inspired by the American league. Her question to followers ended up sparking comments about her own sports preferences.
articles.summary: The golf influencer shared a video to promote a new clothing collection inspired by the American league. Her question to followers ended up sparking comments about her own sports preferences.
articles.body:
Paige Spiranac once again caught the attention of NFL fans, this time because of her sporting preferences. The American influencer posted a video in which she showcased pieces from a new Swag Golf collection inspired by several teams in the league and used the post to ask her followers which one was their favorite.

These are golf accessories designed to protect and carry the equipment used during a round. They include covers to protect the clubs, small bags for storing the little supports where the ball is placed before being struck, and other accessories such as towels and organizers.

The conversation soon shifted to her own loyalties. Spiranac explained that she feels a special fondness for the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Buffalo Bills , two franchises she has expressed support for on different occasions. The choice also sparked comments from fans of other teams who wanted to join the conversation.

Steelers and Bills, two teams among her favorites

Spiranac's connection to Pittsburgh has family roots. Both of her parents are from that city, so she grew up following the Steelers . However, her link to the NFL doesn't end there: she has also expressed her affection for Buffalo .

My parents are from Pittsburgh, so I was born a Steelers fan. Although I can't forget my love for the Bills

A question that sparked debate among the followers

In her most recent post, Spiranac showed different items from the Swag Golf collection with references to NFL franchises. The message accompanying the video was direct: "Which is your favorite team?". The post invited her followers to share their preferences while they viewed the different designs.

The post also prompted some humorous responses. One follower commented that he had always been a fan of the New England Patriots, while another joked that he had stopped supporting the Chicago Bears to become a New England supporter. There were also those who asked why the Miami Dolphins were not among the options.

The variety of teams that appear among her preferences is not new either. In previous posts, the influencer had acknowledged that her fondness for different franchises could be difficult to explain. She even invited her followers to digitally edit her clothing with the colors of their favorite teams and joked that she did not want to receive criticism for her choices.

With this new post linked to Swag Golf, Spiranac once again combined her activity in the world of golf with her interest in American football. The Steelers and the Bills remain the teams she has explicitly mentioned as part of her preferences, while her followers took advantage of the video to defend the colors of their own franchises.

articles.title: DK Metcalf could be the sacrifice Pittsburgh needs to finally fix its dysfunction
articles.standfirst: The wide receiver's ejection against the Eagles was particularly damaging given how little he's contributed offensively throughout the season
articles.summary: The wide receiver's ejection against the Eagles was particularly damaging given how little he's contributed offensively throughout the season
articles.body:
T he Pittsburgh Steelers have reached a crossroads, and according to Sports Illustrated senior writer Conor Orr, the franchise might need to make an uncomfortable decision if it genuinely wants to change its culture: cut DK Metcalf.

Following another disappointing defeat, this time a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Pittsburgh is facing growing questions about its direction under head coach Mike McCarthy. But while the team’s offensive struggles and defensive inconsistencies have been major concerns, Metcalf’s ejection and subsequent departure from the stadium have become a symbol of what Orr believes is a much bigger organizational problem.

In his latest column for Sports Illustrated, Orr argued that the Steelers need to establish accountability rather than continue protecting veteran players and maintaining an environment in which disappointing performances and questionable behavior appear to carry few consequences.

Metcalf’s situation, according to Orr, offers Pittsburgh an opportunity to make a statement. The wide receiver was ejected in the third quarter against Philadelphia after two personal fouls involving Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean . The second incident reportedly involved Metcalf poking DeJean in the eye.

Things became even more controversial after the game when Metcalf reportedly left the stadium immediately following the final whistle, skipping postgame interviews while his teammates were still arriving in the locker room. For Orr, that behavior should have consequences.

Conor Orr questions Pittsburgh’s culture and veteran leadership

Orr’s criticism goes beyond Metcalf’s ejection. He believes Pittsburgh has developed a culture in which veteran status and locker-room relationships appear to matter more than accountability. One of his biggest targets was quarterback Aaron Rodgers , who has repeatedly pushed back against suggestions that the Steelers’ disappointing performances should be considered alarming.

After Pittsburgh’s loss to Cincinnati the previous week, Rodgers dismissed the significance of the defeat. Following the Eagles game, he again resisted describing the situation as “deflating.” Orr suggested that Rodgers has increasingly acted as a defender of the team’s public image rather than someone willing to acknowledge its problems.

The writer also questioned the Steelers’ insistence that their veteran leadership and internal relationships are enough to keep the locker room together. In Orr’s view , that approach has become an excuse for avoiding difficult decisions.

The Metcalf situation is particularly frustrating because of the receiver’s lack of production. Against Philadelphia, he managed just one catch for two yards on four targets. Across his previous four games, according to Orr, Metcalf had recorded only six receptions on 22 targets.

For a player expected to become one of Pittsburgh’s most dangerous offensive weapons, those numbers are difficult to justify, especially considering his substantial financial commitment. Orr argued that cutting Metcalf could send a powerful message to the rest of the roster: nobody is above accountability, regardless of reputation, salary or relationships inside the locker room.

Cutting Metcalf could be the beginning of a bigger change

Orr’s proposal is certainly controversial. Releasing a high-profile wide receiver in the middle of the season would carry financial and football consequences, and it wouldn’t automatically solve Pittsburgh’s offensive problems. But his argument is less about Metcalf’s individual production and more about what the organization is willing to tolerate.

The Steelers have spent years maintaining a reputation for toughness, accountability and organizational stability. However, Orr believes that stability has turned into stagnation, with the franchise seemingly content to remain competitive without making the changes necessary to become a legitimate championship contender.

Metcalf’s ejection and decision to leave the stadium without addressing reporters have provided another example of the frustrations surrounding the team. Rodgers and his teammates might prefer to handle the situation privately, but Orr believes Pittsburgh needs to demonstrate that its standards apply to everyone.

The Steelers could still make the playoffs. They could even win the AFC North if things break their way. But according to Orr, that isn’t the point anymore. If Pittsburgh genuinely wants to change its trajectory, it might have to start by making a difficult decision involving one of its biggest offensive investments.

articles.title: "Give him a beating": Calls to fire DK Metcalf over his costly eye-poke that derails Aaron Rodgers' farewell tour
articles.standfirst: Former Packers quarterback Kurt Benkert led a wave of outrage urging the franchise to cut ties immediately
articles.summary: Former Packers quarterback Kurt Benkert led a wave of outrage urging the franchise to cut ties immediately
articles.body:
P ittsburgh ’s bid to snap a six-decade drought in Philadelphia ended in bitter frustration on Sunday afternoon, and much of the blame landed squarely on the shoulders of star wide receiver DK Metcalf .

With 4:58 remaining in the third quarter of a tight battle at Lincoln Financial Field, quarterback Aaron Rodgers threw an incomplete third-down pass intended for rookie wideout Germie Bernard .

Instead of heading quietly to the sideline, Metcalf escalated an ongoing skirmish with Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean , thrusting his hand through DeJean ’s facemask toward the defender’s eyes.

Officials immediately threw a flag for unsportsmanlike conduct. Because Metcalf had already been penalized earlier in the contest for unnecessary roughness following another run-in with DeJean, the infraction triggered an automatic ejection, the third of Metcalf’s NFL career, tying him with linebacker Dre Greenlaw for the most by any player since 2019.

Watching his former Green Bay Packers teammate Rodgers lose his top perimeter weapon in a winnable road game, retired quarterback Kurt Benkert unleashed a blistering reaction on social media, demanding that Pittsburgh void Metcalf’s deal before another week goes by.

“ DK Metcalf has single-handedly cost the Steelers SO much,” Benkert wrote. “Money, games, coaches jobs, Rodge farewell tour. All of it. I’d cut his a*s tomorrow for conduct detrimental to the team. Get whatever money back you can.”

Why Pittsburgh’s $33 million gamble on Metcalf is unraveling in Aaron Rodgers’ final season

Benkert’s fury reflected widespread exasperation across Pittsburgh following a 19-16 defeat that dropped the Steelers to 6-4, now 1.5 games behind the Cincinnati Bengals in the AFC North, and extended their losing streak in Philadelphia to 12 consecutive games dating back to October 24, 1965.

Even after Metcalf departed with just one reception for two yards on four targets, Pittsburgh’s offense stayed competitive behind practice-squad call-up Max Hurleman , who hauled in six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown, underscoring how costly Metcalf’s lack of composure proved in a three-point game.

For a franchise that surrendered a second-round draft pick to the Seattle Seahawks in March 2025 and handed Metcalf a four-year, $132 million contract extension, the return on investment has become increasingly difficult to defend.

Through 10 games in 2026, Metcalf has caught fewer than half of his 74 targets, totaling just 36 receptions for 434 yards and two touchdowns.

That sluggish output follows a turbulent 2025 campaign in which he finished with 59 catches, 850 yards, and six scores while serving a two-game suspension for striking a fan during a road trip to Detroit.

Local media voices in Pittsburgh echoed Benkert’s call for accountability. On 93.7 The Fan, host Andrew Fillipponi ripped the receiver’s repeated lapses in discipline.

“ DK Metcalf embarrassed the Steelers logo,” Fillipponi said. “He really is an embarrassment to the organization. The fact that this team is paying him $33 million a year and did not make a move last year when he punched a man is disgraceful. He is now a black eye to this team. He is, to me, the biggest punchline, clowning joke around the NFL.”

Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy confirmed after the game that the organization will handle the incident internally, though he did not hide his disappointment.

“We need him,” McCarthy said. “We needed him today, and that was unacceptable.” Worse still for Pittsburgh, NFL insider Benjamin Allbright reported Sunday that the league office is reviewing the eye-poke and could suspend Metcalf as a repeat offender, potentially sidelining him for Friday’s crucial November 27 home matchup against the Denver Broncos and further jeopardizing Rodgers’ final run at a championship.

articles.standfirst: Pittsburgh's $132 million receiver has broken his silence after being ejected against Philadelphia
articles.summary: Pittsburgh's $132 million receiver has broken his silence after being ejected against Philadelphia
articles.body:
DK Metcalf 's controversial ejection against the Philadelphia Eagles has taken another unexpected turn after the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver claimed he couldn't remember the confrontation that resulted in his dismissal.

The 28-year-old was removed during the third quarter of Sunday's 19-16 defeat at Lincoln Financial Field after appearing to reach toward Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean 's eyes during a heated exchange.

Metcalf had already been penalized for an earlier altercation involving DeJean , meaning the second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty brought his afternoon to an abrupt conclusion.

However, when reporters questioned him about the incident on Monday, the receiver offered little explanation for what had happened.

"I can't remember," Metcalf said when asked to describe his interaction with the Philadelphia defender.

Asked whether he believed DeJean had provoked him, Metcalf avoided directly answering the question. "You gotta ask him," he replied.

The Steelers receiver denied deliberately attempting to poke DeJean in the eye, explaining that he had simply been telling his opponent to stop pushing him.

His response attracted further attention because the confrontation had been captured by television cameras and resulted in Pittsburgh losing one of its most important offensive players.

DeJean reveals what happened

DeJean offered a more detailed account following Philadelphia's victory, explaining that the physical battle between the two players had intensified throughout the game.

"We were just competing," DeJean told reporters. "Things like that happen in football. It wasn't anything crazy. No one was really saying anything, it was just two guys going at it."

The Eagles defender confirmed that Metcalf had narrowly missed making contact with his eye, while suggesting that the receiver's frustration may have contributed to the confrontation.

"He wasn't getting the ball a whole lot during that game. Some receivers, they let that get to them. Obviously he tried to take it out on me," DeJean added.

Metcalf finished with just one reception for two yards on four targets, another disappointing return during a season in which his production has fallen below expectations.

The receiver has recorded 36 catches for 434 yards and two touchdowns through 10 appearances, despite signing a four-year, $132 million contract extension in March 2025.

When asked whether he regretted his actions, Metcalf acknowledged the consequences without directly accepting responsibility for the alleged eye-poking incident.

"I just wish I would have been there for my team," he said.

Metcalf disciplinary update before Broncos clash

Pittsburgh head coach Mike McCarthy was visibly frustrated by the dismissal, making clear that the team couldn't afford to lose important players through disciplinary incidents.

"It's emotional on a number of fronts," McCarthy said after the defeat. "We lost a game, a tough game. You take all that in, and everything will be addressed. We can't have players getting ejected from games."

Metcalf 's disciplinary record has become a growing concern, with the receiver leading NFL wideouts in penalties this season.

He also missed the final two regular-season games of 2025 following an altercation with a Detroit Lions fan.

According to NFL insider Adam Schefter, Metcalf won't receive a suspension over Sunday's incident, although the league will continue reviewing his conduct for possible fines.

That leaves him available for Pittsburgh's Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos , providing an opportunity to put the controversy behind him.

However, his unusual explanation and another costly ejection have ensured that questions about his discipline will remain a talking point ahead of the Steelers ' next game.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy refuses to bench Aaron Rodgers despite offense laying an egg against the Eagles
articles.standfirst: The 42-year-old quarterback endured another difficult afternoon as Pittsburgh suffered its second consecutive defeat
articles.summary: The 42-year-old quarterback endured another difficult afternoon as Pittsburgh suffered its second consecutive defeat
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are facing growing pressure to revive their struggling offense after another damaging defeat, but Mike McCarthy has made it clear that Aaron Rodgers won't be the player sacrificed in an attempt to turn their season around.

Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday exposed familiar problems, with the offense struggling to sustain drives, protect its quarterback or generate enough opportunities to seriously threaten the opposition.

Rodgers completed 30 of his 44 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown, but Philadelphia's defense sacked him five times and repeatedly forced Pittsburgh into uncomfortable situations.

The Steelers finished with just 255 total yards and failed to score an offensive touchdown until the fourth quarter, extending their losing streak to two games following their bye week.

Those struggles prompted questions about whether McCarthy might consider benching Rodgers , particularly with younger quarterbacks waiting for an opportunity.

However, the coach delivered an unequivocal response when asked about a possible change on Monday.

"Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback," McCarthy said, according to Steelers reporter Mark Kaboly.

McCarthy 's decision comes at a difficult moment for Pittsburgh, which has slipped to 6-4 and fallen behind both Cincinnati and Cleveland in the AFC North standings.

Rodgers , who turns 43 on December 2, has thrown for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions through 10 appearances this season.

Those figures suggest the veteran remains capable of producing competitive performances, although Pittsburgh's overall offensive output has failed to match expectations.

The Steelers are averaging 310.4 yards and 21.3 points per game, numbers that highlight their difficulty establishing consistent attacking momentum.

Sunday's problems were compounded by the dismissal of wide receiver DK Metcalf , who received two unsportsmanlike conduct penalties following confrontations with Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean .

Metcalf finished with only one reception for two yards before his third-quarter ejection, leaving Rodgers without one of his most important targets.

The quarterback expressed disappointment afterward but declined to reveal the details of his conversation with Metcalf , whom he described as a "real good friend."

McCarthy was less reserved when discussing the consequences of losing a key player through disciplinary action.

"It's emotional on a number of fronts," McCarthy said. "We lost a game, a tough game. You take all that in, and everything will be addressed. We can't have players getting ejected from games."

Steelers face difficult quarterback future

Although Rodgers remains Pittsburgh's undisputed starter, the franchise faces important decisions beyond this season.

The four-time NFL MVP has repeatedly suggested that 2026 will be his final campaign, leaving the Steelers with an uncertain succession plan.

Mason Rudolph currently serves as Rodgers ' primary backup, while Will Howard and Drew Allar represent younger alternatives who have yet to establish themselves in regular-season NFL action.

Neither offers an obvious immediate upgrade, particularly with Pittsburgh attempting to remain competitive in a difficult divisional race.

The Steelers will have little time to address their problems before hosting the Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

Another defeat would further complicate their playoff ambitions, increasing scrutiny of an offense that has struggled to deliver when needed most.

McCarthy 's backing removes any immediate uncertainty surrounding Rodgers ' position, but the veteran quarterback now faces the challenge of demonstrating that Pittsburgh's faith remains justified.
