articles.title: What happens between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy? The Steelers' decision is now under suspicion
articles.standfirst: Pittsburgh stunned the NFL by benching Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: Pittsburgh stunned the NFL by benching Aaron Rodgers
articles.body:
Few moves in recent NFL memory have triggered as much immediate whiplash as the bombshell the Pittsburgh Steelers dropped late Tuesday night.

With a crucial Black Friday matchup against the Denver Broncos (8:00 p.m. GMT / 3:00 p.m. ET) rapidly approaching, the franchise announced not only that veteran backup Mason Rudolph will take over under center, but that future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers will not even suit up.

Steelers spokesperson Burt Lauten delivered the news in a brief, unvarnished official statement that left NFL circles scrambling for answers: “The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for the game this Friday against the Denver Broncos . Aaron Rodgers will be inactive. For the game on Friday.”

What makes the move so baffling is how completely it contradicts everything coming out of Pittsburgh’s facility just a day earlier.

During his weekly press conference slightly more than 24 hours before the announcement, head coach Mike McCarthy reacted with visible puzzlement when asked whether he was considering a change at quarterback, brushing the suggestion aside without hesitation.

“No, Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback,” McCarthy said.

By Tuesday night, however, that certainty had vanished. NFL Network insider Tom Pelissero confirmed that the sudden pivot came straight from the coaching staff rather than an unreported injury, framing it around the 42-year-old quarterback’s recent dip in form: “Stunner, the Steelers are benching Aaron Rodgers and naming Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Sources say this was a coach’s decision. But Rodgers has struggled, and now Mike McCarthy is making a change.”

Why the abrupt reversal points to friction behind closed doors in Pittsburgh

Even accounting for Pittsburgh’s recent offensive sputters, the timeline simply does not add up on football merits alone.

Through 10 games in what has been widely viewed as his farewell NFL campaign, Rodgers has thrown for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions while guiding the Steelers to a 6-4 record, just 1.5 games behind the Cincinnati Bengals in a tight AFC North race.

Admittedly, film from the past two weeks, capped by Sunday’s frustrating 19-16 road loss to the Philadelphia Eagles , in which wideout DK Metcalf was ejected for poking cornerback Cooper DeJean through his facemask, shows Rodgers missing open receivers and looking out of rhythm.

Yet teams do not demote a healthy, iconic quarterback to street clothes overnight strictly over two shaky outings, especially when he practiced normally earlier that very day.

According to Steelers beat reporter Alan Saunders , nothing appeared out of the ordinary during Tuesday’s session: Rodgers took his usual first-team snaps and handled his midweek media obligations just like any other game week.

By the time Tuesday night turned into early Wednesday morning, however, he had been scratched from Friday’s lineup altogether, leaving Pittsburgh to lean on Rudolph alongside young reserves Will Howard and potentially Drew Allar .

For observers around the league, that rapid sequence screams of an off-field flashpoint. Rodgers and McCarthy famously share a complicated history dating back to their 13 seasons together with the Green Bay Packers , a partnership that produced a Super Bowl XLV championship but ended amid well-documented philosophical tension before they reunited in Pittsburgh.

A coach does not move from declaring “No, Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback” to rendering him inactive in roughly a single day unless something significant boiled over behind closed doors, whether a heated disagreement over offensive direction, a clash of egos, or an irreconcilable dispute following Tuesday’s practice.

Pittsburgh has yet to offer any explanation beyond Lauten’s initial release, guaranteeing that McCarthy’s next trip to the podium will be among the most scrutinized press conferences of the 2026 season.

Until the full story surfaces, Rudolph will prepare to lead the Steelers against Denver on Friday, while Rodgers watches his farewell tour stall from the sideline.

articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh Steelers stunned the NFL world by announcing Rodgers' benching in favor of Mason Rudolph on late Tuesday night.
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers stunned the NFL world by announcing Rodgers' benching in favor of Mason Rudolph on late Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers shocked the NFL world late on Tuesday night with a bombshell statement. At 11:10pm ET, the team announced that Mason Rudolph will be the starting quarterback for their Friday game against the Denver Broncos , and Aaron Rodgers will be inactive for the game.

While it's true that Rodgers has struggled this season, particularly in avoiding sacks and connecting on deep passes, no one actually believes Rudolph gives them a better chance to win games. Obviously, Rodgers isn't taking the news too well, which has led to the team excusing him from heading into the facility on Wednesday.

By most accounts, Rodgers' relationship with the franchise is close to beyond repair. Fans have been looking for a potential boiling point that might have been missed, and it seems like one in particular has been found.

Aaron Rodgers took not so subtle shot at Steelers front office for Max Hurleman situation

Following the team's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles last Sunday, Rodgers took a clear shot at the Steelers front office for waiving wide receiver Max Hurleman during final cuts and placing him on the practice squad, instead of the final 53-man roster.

I think everybody felt before the injury in camp that he was a 53 [man roster] guy. I know the guys in our room did for sure. So for him to finally get elevated and go out and play the way he played was not surprising to any of us. But great for his confidence, and a great reminder for the folks upstairs (the front office) what kind of player he is.

Hurleman had a breakout game on Sunday, catching six passes for 61 yards and a touchdown from Rodgers. Hurleman was making his NFL debut and stepped up after DK Metcalf was ejected from the game.

While it sounds like the coaching staff is the one that made the final decision on Rodgers' benching, perhaps the front office played a role as well. Rodgers' comment surely didn't sit well with them.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' brother Jordan absolves Mike McCarthy of blame and places it on Steelers GM Omar Khan
articles.standfirst: After Rodgers was benched by the team in favor of Mason Rudolph, everyone is trying to make sense of the situation, including Rodgers' family.
articles.summary: After Rodgers was benched by the team in favor of Mason Rudolph, everyone is trying to make sense of the situation, including Rodgers' family.
articles.body:
Right now, everyone is trying to make sense of what's going on with the Pittsburgh Steelers . Very late on Tuesday night, the team announced that Aaron Rodgers would be inactive for their upcoming Friday game against the Denver Broncos . Mason Rudolph is slated to start in his place.

Since then, reports have come out claiming Rodgers was excused from coming to Pittsburgh's training facility on Wednesday, as he processes his benching. Initial reports stated the decision to bench Rodgers came directly from the coaching staff, which is somewhat shocking considering Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy have a tremendous amount of respect for each other stemming from their Green Bay Packers days.

That quarterback-head coach relationship is what makes the whole situation ambiguous to many. The QB's brother, Jordan Rodgers , is one of those who doesn't think we're getting the full story right now. Jordan, who works as a college football analyst for ESPN , was brought on to Get Up on Wednesday to try to make sense of his brother's situation.

Is Omar Khan the one to blame for Steelers' current issues and the Aaron Rodgers benching?

In Jordan's eyes, this isn't a McCarthy decision . Instead, he believes general manager Omar Khan is the one to blame for this; both in terms of the final decision and the mediocre state of the roster he built to not maximize Rodgers' talent.

Like him and Mike have been together so long. The conversations have spanned every aspect of what you could with a head coach and a quarterback. So I don't think that was the issue. To me, this has to be an Omar Khan thing. But I look at this roster and I go, I would've been less surprised waking up hearing Will Howard or Drew Allar was the starter. If you need a quarterback that's a little younger, that can move around a little bit more, or you're looking to the future, that would make more sense... This season, the lack of success, to me, is more of an indictment on Omar Khan and how he constructed this roster because they're in the middle of the last dance and rebuild. And it was a bad combination to be in that spot.

Jordan isn't the only one blaming Khan for the Steelers' current dilemma. Many Steelers fans believe it's time for the general manager to leave. Khan has been with the franchise since 2001, but became the GM in 2022 . Since then, they've made the playoffs three times but lost by two touchdowns or more in the first round each time.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers done with Steelers: 2 competing NFL teams that make sense as next destination
articles.standfirst: The quarterback has confirmed he isn’t going back to Pittsburgh after a falling out with head coach Mike McCarthy.
articles.summary: The quarterback has confirmed he isn’t going back to Pittsburgh after a falling out with head coach Mike McCarthy.
articles.body:
The NFL world has been thrown for a loop. On late Tuesday night, the Pittsburgh Steelers put out a statement announcing that Aaron Rodgers would be inactive for the team’s Black Friday game, with Mason Rudolph starting in his place.

A day later, Rodgers confirmed that his time in Pittsburgh is done. A fallout with head coach Mike McCarthy has severed Rodgers’ relationship with the franchise. Given that Rodgers confirmed before the season that 2026 would be his last year, one would assume he’s set to retire. But what if he wants to finish out this season elsewhere ?

Rodgers is still under contract with the Steelers, so they would have to grant his release first. It sounds like that will happen very soon. Once they do, two teams make sense more than any others.

New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles could be options for Aaron Rodgers if he doesn’t want to retire before end of 2026 season

When it comes to teams who are still in contention for a playoff spot and need quarterback help, the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles seem to be the most logical options.

The Patriots don’t know for sure when Drake Maye will be back from a bad ankle injury. The Buffalo Bills have practically run away with the division, but a Wild Card spot is still within reach . New England is currently turning to Tommy DeVito to replace Maye, but he simply isn’t good enough to lead a playoff charge.

As for the Eagles, their season seemed totally dead a few weeks ago, but a win over Rodgers’ Steelers last Sunday has them still dreaming of a potential playoff berth . The NFC East is far from being clinched by the New York Giants , and the Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders are jumbled together.

All of the other teams in the NFL who could use a quarterback like Rodgers have no hope of making the playoffs. Rodgers would probably rather retire than go somewhere where he won’t be playing for anything meaningful over these last seven weeks of the season.

articles.title: War erupts in Pittsburgh: Aaron Rodgers gets support from Steelers players on Mike McCarthy allegations: ‘It’s all true’
articles.standfirst: Aaron Rodgers broke his silence and made explosive accusations against Mike McCarthy.
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers broke his silence and made explosive accusations against Mike McCarthy.
articles.body:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers dropped a bombshell by launching strong criticism at head coach Mike McCarthy , questioning his preparation, leadership, and overall commitment to the team.

Following his comments, several Pittsburgh players reportedly confirmed to NFL reporters that the veteran quarterback’s most serious accusations are true, increasing the pressure on the head coach.

Mike McCarthy finds himself at the center of the controversy

On Tuesday, the Steelers announced that Rodgers would be benched and inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos—a decision that raised questions about McCarthy’s future with the team.

The next day, Rodgers appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and revealed details about the internal situation in Pittsburgh. The quarterback claimed that McCarthy had already lost the support of several players and that one particular episode at halftime proved to be “the final straw.”

“And I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime, towards the end of it, we’re kind of on the offense on one side of defense on the other side,” Rodgers said. “And there’s some rambling or something, and without even a heads-up, he says, ‘All right, one, two, three, Packers.’”

The reference to the Packers— McCarthy’s former team and the franchise where Rodgers spent 18 seasons —reportedly caused significant friction in the locker room.

According to ESPN’s Brooke Pryor, multiple league sources confirmed the quarterback’s account.

“One source texted: ‘It’s all true.’ Another source told ESPN that McCarthy ‘crossed’ Rodgers, leading to the quarterback’s account Wednesday.”

Rodgers also alleged that McCarthy had been seen sleeping during team meetings and that he displayed unpredictable emotional reactions.

Additionally, reporters from The Athletic cited a Steelers player who backed up the quarterback’s version of events from his McAfee interview.

“Another player said: ‘If you want to know what happened, just turn on the TV,’ referring to Rodgers’ interview with McAfee, which was on the screens of many players when the Steelers locker room opened to the media Wednesday afternoon.”

Is Mike McCarthy’s job at risk?

With Rodgers now out of the organization, some analysts believe McCarthy could also be in danger of losing his position as Pittsburgh’s head coach.

Although the Steelers are still in the playoff hunt, uncertainty is growing over whether McCarthy will remain in charge beyond this season.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy responds to Aaron Rodgers’ allegations and admits ‘1-2-3 Packers’ moment was ‘embarrassing’
articles.standfirst: Aaron Rodgers’ explosive accusations put Mike McCarthy’s future in Pittsburgh in question, with NFL insiders now not ruling out a shocking Steelers coaching change.
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers’ explosive accusations put Mike McCarthy’s future in Pittsburgh in question, with NFL insiders now not ruling out a shocking Steelers coaching change.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy addressed the controversial accusation from Aaron Rodgers about the moment he allegedly ended a team meeting with a “1, 2, 3, Packers!” chant during halftime of Sunday’s game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

When asked about the alleged misstep, McCarthy did not deny that the episode occurred. Instead, he described the situation as an “embarrassing” moment and explained that it happened during an intense locker-room discussion in Philadelphia.

The coach also did not directly respond to Rodgers’ claim that he had fallen asleep during team meetings. However, by acknowledging the “1, 2, 3, Packers” incident, his comments appear to lend greater weight to one of the quarterback’s main criticisms.

Although McCarthy framed it as a mistake made in an emotional moment, the episode represents a blow to his image in Pittsburgh. The coach now faces the challenge of regaining the trust of a locker room shaken by Rodgers’ comments.

The quarterback’s statements triggered a wave of reaction across the NFL. Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk appeared on a Pittsburgh radio station and raised a scenario that once seemed unthinkable: the possibility that McCarthy could lose his job as head coach.

Mike Florio does not rule out Mike McCarthy’s dismissal

Andrew Fillipponi of 93.7 The Fan shared Florio’s comments on social media after his appearance on the show.

“Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk says on @937thefan he does NOT rule out Mike McCarthy being fired by the Steelers,” Fillipponi wrote on X.

As of Tuesday night, the situation inside Pittsburgh had appeared stable. However, the team surprised everyone by announcing that Aaron Rodgers would be benched and inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos .

That decision was followed by the quarterback’s explosive interview on The Pat McAfee Show , in which he publicly questioned McCarthy’s leadership and cast doubt on whether the coach still has the necessary support to maintain control of the Steelers’ locker room.

articles.standfirst: With his Pittsburgh career already over, the quarterback has a chance to take an extraordinary route back into the AFC North rivalry
articles.summary: With his Pittsburgh career already over, the quarterback has a chance to take an extraordinary route back into the AFC North rivalry
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers no longer needs to wait for the Pittsburgh Steelers to decide his future as the AFC North side released him on Wednesday, following an explosive conflict with Mike McCarthy and leaving the veteran available to be claimed before he can enter free agency in the final weeks of the season. Rodgers was let go one day after the team named Mason Rudolph their starter and his next destination remains uncertain - yet the Baltimore Ravens have become a focus of fan speculation because injuries have disrupted their quarterback room with Lamar Jackson out.

At the same time, the fit could make sense as Rodgers has an obvious incentive to face Pittsburgh again and the idea gathered momentum on social media after a fan suggested he should seek a move to Baltimore , potentially setting up two meetings with the Steelers in the closing weeks. Few endings would be more pointed than helping Pittsburgh 's divisional rival damage its NFL Playoffs hopes and although unconfirmed, that possibility is no longer dependent on a hypothetical release after Rodgers ' departure on November 25, following his public criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy after being benched. Rodgers had already said he would not return, and the Steelers made the split official and the Ravens ' injury problems explain why the suggestion has caught on with Jackson is on injured reserve after surgery on his right thumb and back-up Tyler Huntley is also sidelined with a toe injury.

The Ravens' quarterback crisis makes the idea tempting

Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett earlier this month, and he has taken over as starter and to give the Ravens an experienced quarterback and keep its season alive, and the team has already spent draft capital to acquire him. Rodgers offers a bigger name and someone of his talent cannot be ignored – although another change could put the team on the backfoot heading into a vital stage of the ongoing campaign if they hope to clinch the top seed in the AFC North or an AFC Wild Card slot. But the potential attraction extends beyond the quarterback room as Zay Flowers remains one of Baltimore 's leading receiving threats, and a passer with Rodgers ' experience could offer another way to attack downfield and exploit coverage. Still, a new arrival would have little time to build chemistry with the receiver. Flowers has caught 57 passes for 785 yards and three touchdowns during the regular season and those numbers show he is already central to the offense; but his form has dipped of late as the quality of quarterback throwing the ball to him has also substantially degraded. The question of whether a different quarterback could make the connection more consistent during Baltimore 's late-season push is an open one and that’s where Rodgers , a four-time MVP and Super Bowl winner, could potentially come into the picture as he heads through the waiver process.

articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh head coach revealed an ultimatum over his responsibilities played a decisive role in the breakdown of their relationship
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh head coach revealed an ultimatum over his responsibilities played a decisive role in the breakdown of their relationship
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy has offered a different explanation for the collapse of his relationship with Aaron Rodgers , suggesting the quarterback's demands over offensive responsibilities ultimately left him with little choice but to remove the veteran from the Pittsburgh Steelers ' starting lineup. The coach also addressed several accusations that have threatened to overshadow the Steelers ' season as speaking to reporters on Wednesday, McCarthy confirmed that Rodgers had issued an ultimatum that he believed went beyond the quarterback's responsibilities.

Although he refused to disclose the details of their private conversations, he made clear that the decision to bench the four-time MVP was entirely his. "There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of his job description, so it was my decision to bench him," McCarthy explained as the coach also insisted that the management supported his decision, rejecting the suggestion that he had been forced into removing the quarterback from the lineup. Meanwhile Rodgers had presented a considerably different account earlier during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, where he claimed his concerns about McCarthy 's preparation had continued for months, eventually prompting him to request changes including who controlled play-calling responsibilities. The quarterback described several incidents in which he alleged McCarthy had missed meetings, arrived late or fallen asleep during important discussions and also questioned whether the coach was sufficiently familiar with the team's game plan, arguing that the situation had become damaging to the entire organization.

McCarthy addresses Rodgers' most embarrassing accusation

And one particular incident from Pittsburgh 's defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles became a major talking point during Wednesday's press conference as Rodgers alleged that he accidentally ended a halftime team address by shouting "1, 2, 3, Packers!", seemingly confusing his current team with his former Green Bay employers. McCarthy acknowledged that the incident happened, although he challenged Rodgers ' interpretation of the circumstances surrounding it but rather than denying the mistake, the coach described the halftime exchange as emotional and admitted that the moment had been embarrassing. "Half-time was very emotional, and there was conversations prior to that embarrassing moment, but I just think, we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments," McCarthy said as the Steelers coach also attempted to address suggestions that his locker room control had deteriorated. He revealed that he had held a meeting with the team's leadership council earlier on Wednesday, describing the conversation as direct and honest while expressing appreciation for the players who participated. "It was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous things that have been on their mind," McCarthy explained as he added that he was encouraged by the urgency coming out of the discussion. McCarthy also dismissed the suggestion that lingering resentment from their Packers split had influenced his treatment of Rodgers , and, despite the controversy, he remains adamant that he can turn Pittsburgh 's situation around. "I know how to win. And that's the facts. This is my third program, and I plan on winning here," McCarthy declared whilst Rodgers , meanwhile, has already been released after Pittsburgh confirmed Mason Rudolph would replace him against the Denver Broncos in Week 12.

articles.title: Dianna Russini dives straight into the Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy drama and says the Giants dodged a bullet by picking Jaxson Dart in the NFL Draft
articles.standfirst: The New York Giants almost signed the four-time NFL MVP but opted for their talented youngster instead
articles.summary: The New York Giants almost signed the four-time NFL MVP but opted for their talented youngster instead
articles.body:
D ianna Russini has pointed to the New York Giants as a team that may be quietly relieved by Aaron Rodgers ' Pittsburgh Steelers meltdown, arguing that their decision to draft Jaxson Dart rather than pursue the veteran quarterback more aggressively now looks significant. The timing is striking as Rodgers ' turbulent exit from the Steelers reached a new level on Wednesday, November 25, when Pittsburgh released him after he publicly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy .

The split followed his benching and an explosive appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, where he questioned the coach's preparation and Russini took to X.com, formerly Twitter, earlier that day to revisit New York 's quarterback search two offseasons ago. That was when the Giants were reportedly exploring options that included Rodgers after moving on from Daniel Jones , as the MetLife Stadium side found itself still trying to replace Eli Manning . The controversial reporter wrote that the team could be watching events unfold “with a sense of relief” as Russini noting that “New York ultimately opted to draft Jaxson Dart instead.”

Russini's Giants take overlooks the team's veteran signings

The Giants signed Jameis Winston and Russell Wilson in March 2025 before selecting Dart in the first round of that year's draft as their plan was not to rely exclusively on a rookie; the veteran additions were intended to provide immediate quarterback options while the franchise invested in a younger passer. New York had also pursued Stafford before he remained with the Los Angeles Rams , while Rodgers was among the experienced quarterbacks considered during the search, as the Giants ultimately assembled a room featuring Wilson , Winston and Dart , giving them both short-term alternatives and a potential future starter. Rodgers , meanwhile, initially enjoyed a productive first season in Pittsburgh after joining the Steelers following his departure from the New York Jets . He helped lead the team to the playoffs in 2025, reviving hopes that the four-time MVP could still deliver at a high level late in his career. That picture changed this season as Rodgers was benched in favor of Mason Rudolph after Pittsburgh 's recent defeats, then used his interview with Pat McAfee to accuse McCarthy of missing meetings, falling asleep during preparations and mishandling the team. Those claims were Rodgers ' account of the dispute as the quarterback revisited their Green Bay history, where they worked together for 13 seasons and won Super Bowl XLV . Additionally, McCarthy acknowledged the embarrassing “1-2-3 Packers” halftime incident but disputed parts of his former player’s account. The veteran coach said the quarterback had issued an ultimatum over play-calling and Pittsburgh released Rodgers later on Wednesday, leaving Rudolph set to take over as the Steelers move forward.

articles.title: Terrell Owens lashes out at NFL hypocrisy in dispute between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy: “They’d call me a cancer”
articles.standfirst: Rodgers made explosive allegations against Steelers head coach McCarthy
articles.summary: Rodgers made explosive allegations against Steelers head coach McCarthy
articles.body:
Terrell Owens spent much of his NFL career defending his character against accusations that he was a disruptive presence in the locker room. Watching Aaron Rodgers publicly dismantle his relationship with Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy has convinced the former wide receiver that those same standards aren't applied equally across the league.

Owens weighed in after Rodgers delivered an extraordinary interview on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, criticizing McCarthy over his conduct and the circumstances surrounding his benching ahead of Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos .

While Rodgers' allegations subsequently received support from several NFL sources, Owens questioned whether the media would have afforded him similar treatment had he publicly criticized a head coach during his playing career.

“But if I did some s**t what Aaron Rodgers is doing right now, it’d be called conduct detrimental to the team. I’d be insubordinate; I would be a distraction; I’d be called a cancer,” Owens said during a social media livestream.

“But why can he do it and he ain’t getting crucified? But if I did it, or somebody of color did it, they’d be getting raked across the coast.”

Owens revisits painful memories of NFL career

The controversy brought back memories of Owens ' troubled relationship with former San Francisco 49ers quarterback Jeff Garcia , whose alleged conduct during team meetings became a point of contention for the wide receiver before his departure from the franchise.

Owens drew comparisons between his previous grievances and Rodgers ' accusations against McCarthy , arguing that his reputation suffered when he raised concerns about people within his organization.

“This is some privileged stuff right here. This is some double standard stuff right here,” Owens continued.

The six-time Pro Bowl receiver maintained that public perceptions of his personality were heavily influenced by media coverage, which he believes frequently misrepresented the circumstances surrounding his disagreements with teammates and coaches.

“But what I have been saying all along is that there’s a double standard, and I was treated unfairly. I was viewed differently. My character was attacked,” Owens added.

Rodgers was waived by Pittsburgh on Wednesday after alleging that McCarthy had fallen asleep during meetings, missed team activities and failed to personally inform him of his demotion.

Sources cited by ESPN subsequently supported the quarterback's account, with one telling reporter Brooke Pryor: “It's all true.”

Pittsburgh must now navigate the consequences of Rodgers ' departure, while Owens has reignited a longstanding debate about the relationship between player accountability, media coverage and race in professional football.

articles.title: Nobody loves Aaron Rodgers? Fans mercilessly tear into the fired QB: “He’s got more baggage than O’Hare Airport before Christmas”
articles.standfirst: Have performances and off-field disagreements damaged his chances of finding another team?
articles.summary: Have performances and off-field disagreements damaged his chances of finding another team?
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has spent much of his NFL career commanding the attention of opposing defenses, but the legendary quarterback is now struggling to attract interest of a different kind. Following his abrupt departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers , the prospect of an unwanted ending to his illustrious career has become increasingly realistic.

The Steelers waived Rodgers on Wednesday, following his public criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy , leaving the 42-year-old quarterback without a team during what was expected to be his final NFL season.

However, a concerning update from NFL insider Dianna Russini suggested that Rodgers might struggle to find another employer, despite his considerable accomplishments and the number of franchises dealing with quarterback uncertainty.

“I’ve asked around about Aaron Rodgers with multiple teams. Right now, there’s no taker. Injuries can change situations in an instant, but in what’s supposed to be his final season, his options appear limited,” Russini wrote on X.

The revelation prompted a particularly unforgiving response from some football supporters, who questioned whether Rodgers ' reputation and recent performances justified the potential complications of signing him.

“He has more baggage at this point than O'Hare airport a few days before Christmas. Who needs the drama?” one fan commented. “He is exiting the league the same way he entered. Waiting for someone to call his number…” another supporter wrote.

“He is exiting the league the same way he entered. Waiting for someone to call his number…” a third supporter said.

Declining performances could complicate NFL return

Beyond the controversy surrounding his departure, Rodgers ' performances this season provide prospective employers with another reason to approach the situation cautiously.

The veteran completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions across 10 starts, recording a career-low passer rating of 86.6. He was also sacked 31 times.

Pittsburgh had lost consecutive games against Cincinnati and Philadelphia after opening the season with a 6-2 record, although McCarthy initially appeared committed to retaining Rodgers as his starting quarterback.

That changed when Mason Rudolph was promoted ahead of the Steelers ' Black Friday encounter with the Denver Broncos , prompting Rodgers to publicly criticize McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show.

Rodgers alleged that his coach had fallen asleep during meetings and failed to personally inform him of his benching. Reports of disagreements over offensive playcalling subsequently emerged, further illustrating the deterioration of their relationship.

Fans believe Rodgers should consider retirement

The uncertainty surrounding Rodgers ' future has also divided supporters in Green Bay, where the quarterback delivered a Super Bowl championship and established himself among the franchise's greatest players.

“I think his time was up last year,” Packers supporter Michelle Benz told NBC 26. “He should have left the game last year.”

Others remain hopeful that Rodgers can secure a more fitting conclusion to his career, including fellow Packers fan Matt Kadlec : “I obviously want him to go out on top, I don't want to see him fail. But I'm grateful for him.”

With the Thanksgiving Day waiver deadline set for 4 p.m. ET, Rodgers could soon become a free agent. Whether another franchise considers his experience worth the potential complications remains the defining question surrounding his NFL future.

articles.title: The dream QB showdown that never happened: Aaron Rodgers could retire without ever playing against Patrick Mahomes
articles.standfirst: Injuries and illness have repeatedly prevented two of the greatest quarterbacks of the modern era from meeting
articles.summary: Injuries and illness have repeatedly prevented two of the greatest quarterbacks of the modern era from meeting
articles.body:
Football fans have spent nearly a decade watching Aaron Rodgers and Patrick Mahomes produce some of the most memorable quarterback performances in NFL history, yet circumstances have repeatedly conspired to prevent the two Super Bowl winners from sharing the field as opponents.

That fascinating piece of NFL history has taken on renewed significance following Rodgers ' reported departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers , with the 42-year-old potentially approaching the end of his professional career without ever competing against the Kansas City Chiefs superstar.

Rodgers reportedly requested his release on Wednesday after head coach Mike McCarthy decided to replace him with Mason Rudolph ahead of Pittsburgh's Black Friday encounter with the Denver Broncos .

The four-time MVP had recorded 2,241 passing yards, 16 touchdowns and six interceptions this season, helping the Steelers establish a 6-4 record before his relationship with the organization deteriorated.

Should Pittsburgh's recent 19-16 defeat against the Philadelphia Eagles prove to be Rodgers ' final NFL appearance, one of the most anticipated quarterback matchups of the modern era will have never materialized.

Unfortunate twists prevented pair from meeting

The first opportunity arrived in 2019, when Rodgers was still leading the Green Bay Packers and Mahomes was establishing himself as the NFL's premier young quarterback.

However, a dislocated kneecap sidelined Mahomes , leaving Matt Moore to start for Kansas City as Rodgers guided Green Bay to a 31-24 victory.

Another opportunity emerged in 2021, only for Rodgers to miss the game after testing positive for COVID-19. Jordan Love subsequently started for the Packers , with Mahomes leading the Chiefs to a 13-7 victory.

The most recent missed opportunity came in 2023, when Rodgers ' highly anticipated move to the New York Jets was disrupted by an Achilles injury during his debut. Zach Wilson instead started against Kansas City, with the Chiefs securing a 23-20 win.

“Aaron Rodgers might finish career having never played Patrick Mahomes despite being in the league for ten years together,” Pro Football Focus' Daire Carragher wrote on X.

Remarkably, their paths have never crossed in the playoffs either, despite their respective championship successes and extensive postseason experience.

Rodgers running out of time to face Mahomes

The contrasting fortunes of the two quarterbacks make the possibility of a future meeting increasingly uncertain. Mahomes remains firmly in championship contention with Kansas City, while Rodgers must determine whether another opportunity exists elsewhere in the NFL.

The Chiefs entered their Thanksgiving encounter with Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills boasting an 8-2 record, having comfortably defeated the Arizona Cardinals the previous week.

Rodgers , meanwhile, is navigating uncertainty during his 22nd NFL season, which was already widely expected to be his last before the developments in Pittsburgh.

Even if another franchise signs the veteran quarterback, there is no guarantee that its schedule or postseason journey would bring him into direct competition with Mahomes .

After 274 regular-season appearances, Rodgers has little left to prove. Nevertheless, retirement could leave one particularly intriguing chapter of modern NFL history unwritten.

articles.standfirst: Retirement is approaching for the legendary quarterback
articles.summary: Retirement is approaching for the legendary quarterback
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers may have played his final game for the Pittsburgh Steelers , but the veteran quarterback still has unfinished business in the NFL. Among the more remarkable omissions from his illustrious career is that he has never competed against Patrick Mahomes , despite the two quarterbacks spending 10 seasons in the league together.

Rodgers ' hopes of changing that statistic appeared to diminish considerably on Wednesday when Pittsburgh waived him following his public criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy on The Pat McAfee Show.

The 42-year-old had already indicated that 2026 would be his final season, while a career-low passer rating of 86.6 has raised questions about whether another franchise would consider signing him.

Nevertheless, quarterback injuries have created potential openings elsewhere in the league, with Sports Illustrated identifying the Baltimore Ravens, New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals as three possible destinations.

None has publicly expressed interest in Rodgers , but each presents circumstances that could offer the former Super Bowl champion an opportunity to postpone retirement.

Ravens and Patriots offer potential playoff lifeline

Baltimore would represent a particularly intriguing destination given its longstanding rivalry with Pittsburgh and the circumstances surrounding Rodgers ' departure. The Ravens still have two regular season games against the Steelers , scheduled for Weeks 15 and 18.

Injuries to Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley have disrupted Baltimore's quarterback plans, while Jacoby Brissett has lost both starts since joining the organization. Despite six consecutive defeats, the Ravens remain mathematically involved in the AFC playoff race at 4-7.

New England could offer Rodgers a stronger competitive platform, with the Patriots sitting at 5-5 despite losing starting quarterback Drake Maye to a fractured fibula.

Mike Vrabel has committed to Tommy DeVito during Maye 's absence, although Rodgers ' longstanding relationship with Patriots executive Eliot Wolf , established during their time together in Green Bay, provides an interesting connection.

Joining either AFC franchise could theoretically create a postseason meeting with Mahomes , provided the respective teams qualify and their playoff paths intersect.

Cardinals complicate Patrick Mahomes reunion hopes

Arizona presents a different opportunity for Rodgers , whose previous working relationship with offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett could make the transition into an unfamiliar organization considerably easier.

Hackett worked alongside Rodgers in Green Bay and New York, while Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur is the younger brother of Matt LaFleur , who coached Rodgers for four seasons with the Packers .

Arizona has also experienced significant quarterback problems, with injuries to Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck forcing veteran Josh Johnson into the starting lineup.

However, the Cardinals have already faced Kansas City this season, and their 3-8 record makes a potential Super Bowl meeting extremely unlikely.

Rodgers ' immediate challenge remains finding a franchise willing to extend his career. Unless an opportunity emerges, the quarterback showdown that has eluded football fans for nearly a decade could remain one of the NFL's greatest missed encounters.

articles.title: Tom Brady rips Aaron Rodgers and delivers a scathing moral lesson over Mike McCarthy comments
articles.standfirst: Tom Brady delivers a powerful locker room message after Aaron Rodgers’ McCarthy criticism.
articles.summary: Tom Brady delivers a powerful locker room message after Aaron Rodgers’ McCarthy criticism.
articles.body:
Despite being an NFL legend—and perhaps the greatest quarterback ever to play in the league— Tom Brady had to spend this holiday working the broadcast of the Philadelphia Eagles vs. Dallas Cowboys game. During the telecast, he delivered a strong statement regarding Aaron Rodgers’ recent comments about Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy .

What did Tom Brady say about Aaron Rodgers’ comments?

“The sanctity of the NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we shouldn’t ever lose track of that as players. It’s a privilege to be in that locker room. You’re fighting with your teammates, you’re fighting with your coaches, you’re always acting as a team together,” the legendary former quarterback said.

Four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers appeared on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon to address his unexpected benching—and he did not hold back when explaining his side of the story or his feelings toward head coach Mike McCarthy .

Rodgers revealed that he learned he would be inactive through a phone call with teammate Pat Freiermuth , rather than directly from the coaching staff.

“I found out that I was gonna be inactive on a phone call last night from Pat Freiermuth,” Rodgers said in the interview. “I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, ‘I can’t believe they’re doing this.’ And I said, ‘Doing what?’ I didn’t know. And he told me, and obviously, there had been a lot of things in motion at that point. I didn’t hear from Mike [McCarthy].”

“Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, and that word [benching] never came up,” Rodgers continued.

“Last Wednesday, we’re in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring,” Rodgers said. “Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened.”

Rodgers also accused McCarthy of skipping an offensive meeting the following day and missing the team’s Friday walkthrough.

“Doesn’t come to the first walkthrough. Doesn’t come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday. Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don’t have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly. And then comes Sunday, when obviously we struggled, and the product wasn’t great.”

Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. Less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened.”
Rodgers also accused McCarthy of skipping an offensive meeting the following day and missing the team’s Friday walkthrough.

articles.title: NFL legend brands Aaron Rodgers a "jerk" following feud with Mike McCarthy
articles.standfirst: Former New York Giants superstar Michael Strahan questioned Rodgers' attitude and leadership
articles.summary: Former New York Giants superstar Michael Strahan questioned Rodgers' attitude and leadership
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers ' decision to cite his considerable career earnings while explaining why he felt comfortable publicly criticizing Mike McCarthy struck a nerve with Michael Strahan , who delivered a particularly blunt assessment of the quarterback's conduct during Fox Sports' Thanksgiving coverage.

The former New York Giants defensive end believes Rodgers crossed an unacceptable boundary when he aired his grievances against the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach on The Pat McAfee Show, disregarding the potential consequences for the teammates he was leaving behind.

Rodgers was waived by Pittsburgh on Wednesday, just hours after accusing McCarthy of falling asleep during meetings, missing scheduled team activities and failing to personally inform him of his benching.

Although Strahan acknowledged that McCarthy wasn't necessarily blameless, he insisted that disagreements between players and coaches should be resolved privately rather than becoming a distraction for the entire organization.

“It’s sad,” Strahan said. “As a player, you just don’t air those things. We’ve all had disagreements, but you just don’t publicly air those things like this.”

Rodgers ' suggestion that earning approximately $400 million during his NFL career afforded him the freedom to speak openly particularly frustrated Strahan , who believed the quarterback's financial security was irrelevant to his responsibilities as a teammate.

“You’re a rich jerk. You’re a rich, bad teammate,” Strahan declared. “There always seems to be smoke around Aaron Rodgers, and as my parents used to say, where there’s smoke, there’s fire.”

Having spent all 15 seasons of his NFL career with the Giants , Strahan emphasized that individual grievances should never undermine the collective interests of a football team.

“What you did, which is disappointing to me, is you hurt your team,” Strahan continued. “It’s about the team. We are playing a team sport, which you cannot play as an individual, and that’s what he’s doing.”

The criticism comes as Pittsburgh prepares to continue its playoff pursuit with Mason Rudolph at quarterback following Rodgers ' departure.

Jerry Jones challenges Aaron Rodgers' allegations

Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones also entered the discussion following his team's Thanksgiving defeat against Philadelphia, disputing Rodgers ' suggestion that similar problems had occurred during McCarthy's five seasons in Dallas.

“No, I never saw anything,” Jones said when asked about the allegations. “I offered him to stay at least another year when he left. He’s frankly one of the finest people around football that I’ve been around.”

Meanwhile, Rodgers cleared waivers on Thursday, officially becoming a free agent less than a week before his 43rd birthday.

Having previously indicated that 2026 would be his final season, the four-time MVP now faces the possibility of retirement without another NFL appearance, leaving his public confrontation with McCarthy as one of the defining moments of his final campaign.

articles.title: “We weren’t prepared for this”: Jordan Rodgers reveals how his brother Aaron’s shocking release from the Steelers shook his family
articles.standfirst: Aaron’s sudden release leaves his family stunned as Jordan speaks out against McCarthy
articles.summary: Aaron’s sudden release leaves his family stunned as Jordan speaks out against McCarthy
articles.body:
Jordan Rodgers has opened up about his family’s reaction to Aaron Rodgers’ unexpected departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers , admitting they weren’t prepared for the dramatic events that brought his brother’s time with the franchise to an abrupt end.

Appearing on Good Morning America on Friday, the 38-year-old television personality discussed the growing controversy surrounding Aaron and Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy .

Jordan described the situation as an upsetting development, particularly given the excitement surrounding their reunion in Pittsburgh.

“I think that first and foremost, it’s just kind of sad to see it end this way in Pittsburgh with so much good vibes and hopes about the reuniting of McCarthy and Rodgers and the potential to make a playoff run, one last dance,” Jordan said.

McCarthy previously coached Aaron for 13 seasons with the Green Bay Packers, from 2006 until 2018. Their reunion in Pittsburgh had generated considerable optimism, with the quarterback initially signing a one-year contract in 2025 before returning for another season.

However, tensions escalated after the Steelers announced Mason Rudolph would start their Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos. Aaron later appeared on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, making several allegations about McCarthy's conduct.

The quarterback claimed the coach had missed team activities and fallen asleep during meetings. He also recalled an incident during halftime when McCarthy allegedly interrupted the locker-room discussion by saying, “1-2-3 Packers.”

Aaron was released by Pittsburgh later that day, leaving him without a team.

Jordan Rodgers questions Mike McCarthy’s future with the Steelers

Jordan was particularly critical of the allegations against McCarthy , arguing that such behavior would be unacceptable in professional football.

“I think what’s getting lost in this though is just how unacceptable and unprecedented some of the behavior that McCarthy has displayed and how unique that is, and I think that I would be surprised if he continued to be the head coach moving forward,” Jordan stated.

“Having been in locker rooms, having been a third-string quarterback on a practice squad … if I even looked like I was nodding off, I’d be cut in a second.

“And to have that happen from the head coach, a play caller, you can’t play football that way and there’s too many jobs at stake for people to put up with that type of behavior.”

McCarthy , meanwhile, has declined to publicly discuss his private conversations with Aaron , maintaining that he's still the right person to lead the franchise.

Steelers owner Art Rooney I I has also thrown his support behind the coach, declaring his full confidence in McCarthy and expecting him to remain in the position beyond the current season. Rooney additionally stressed that insubordination and ultimatums couldn't be tolerated within the organization.

Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin has also expressed disappointment, describing the franchise's situation as a “dumpster fire.” He admitted he was shocked that disagreements between two people he knows well had become such a public spectacle.

Tomlin also acknowledged that the controversy could create considerable challenges for McCarthy moving forward.

With Rudolph preparing to lead Pittsburgh against Denver, attention has shifted towards the team's ability to recover from the turmoil.

articles.title: The Steelers secure their biggest win of the season against the Broncos after the Aaron Rodgers saga
articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh defense dominated the Broncos, forcing three turnovers
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh defense dominated the Broncos, forcing three turnovers
articles.body:
Following a turbulent week dominated by the sudden exit of Aaron Rodgers, who was released after aiming pointed criticism at head coach Mike McCarthy in the wake of back-to-back defeats, the Pittsburgh Steelers entered Friday’s Week 12 Black Friday showcase at home widely viewed as underdogs against the 8-2 Denver Broncos .

Instead of folding under the weight of locker-room drama, Pittsburgh improved to 7-4 with a statement 27-5 victory , producing the first scorigami of that exact final score in NFL history .

Powered by a relentless defense that scored twice, including a safety and a pick-six, alongside an efficient outing from new starting quarterback Mason Rudolph , who hooked up with DK Metcalf for a crucial opening-quarter score, the Steelers silenced the outside noise in emphatic fashion.

Steelers Defense Dominates Rainy Clash as Rudolph Connects With Metcalf

Playing in steady rain in Pittsburgh, the Steelers defense suffocated Denver from the opening kickoff, holding the Broncos to just 68 total yards in the first half and 205 total yards on 3.0 yards per play for the afternoon.

Veteran cornerback Jalen Ramsey delivered the signature blow late in the second quarter by intercepting Bo Nix and weaving 36 yards into the end zone to stretch the lead to 24-5 before halftime, while rookie defensive back Daylen Everette sealed the three-turnover clinic with a fourth-quarter pick against Nix ( 169 passing yards, two interceptions, 44.7 passer rating ) on fourth-and-21.

Against one of the league’s stingiest units, Mason Rudolph avoided costly mistakes and finished 9-of-15 passing for 142 yards , zero interceptions, and a 113.8 passer rating , spreading completions to seven different targets while Rico Dowdle paced the ground attack with 71 rushing yards on 11 carries.

Rudolph’s sharpest throw came in the first quarter, when he dropped a 22-yard touchdown pass into the hands of DK Metcalf over All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II (Metcalf finished with three catches for 36 yards), complemented by Chris Boswell’s 2-for-2 field goal kicking. With the turbulence of the Rodgers saga firmly in the rearview mirror,

Pittsburgh now turns its focus to a prime-time Sunday Night Football clash against the Houston Texans on December 6 as it continues to solidify its AFC playoff standing.
